q: The PN is reinforcing safe infant sleep teaching. Which statement by the parent indicates correct understanding?
options: The baby should sleep on the stomach with soft blankets
The baby sleeps on the back, on a firm mattress with nothing soft in the crib
The baby can share our bed if we are light sleepers
Bumper pads make the crib safer
explain: Correct: B - back to sleep, firm mattress, bare crib reduces SIDS risk. A is wrong - prone sleeping and soft bedding increase SIDS risk. C is wrong - bed-sharing raises suffocation and SIDS risk. D is wrong - bumpers are a suffocation hazard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with a seizure disorder is being discharged. Which home safety point should the PN reinforce?
options: Swim alone to build independence
Avoid showers and take only tub baths
Take showers rather than tub baths, avoid heights and unsupervised swimming, and take medication as prescribed
Stop medication once seizures have not occurred for a month
explain: Correct: C - showers reduce drowning risk, heights and solo swimming are hazards, and adherence prevents seizures. A is wrong - swimming alone risks drowning during a seizure. B is wrong - tub baths are the drowning hazard, not showers. D is wrong - stopping antiepileptics without provider direction invites rebound seizures.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is teaching about scald prevention for a family with young children. The PN should reinforce setting the water heater to:
options: 160 F for better dish sterilization
No higher than 120 F
140 F to save energy
The maximum setting for faster hot water
explain: Correct: B - 120 F or below prevents tap-water scalds in children. A, C, and D all risk serious burns; hotter settings scald small children in seconds.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with an implanted pacemaker is scheduled for an MRI. What should the PN do?
options: Send the client to MRI as scheduled
Report the pacemaker to the RN before the MRI; metal devices can be dangerous in the MRI scanner
Remove the pacemaker at the bedside
Tell the client the pacemaker will improve the images
explain: Correct: B - implanted metal/electronic devices are major MRI safety risks requiring screening and RN/provider review. A is wrong - proceeding without screening is dangerous. C is wrong - the PN never removes implanted devices. D is wrong and nonsensical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client's restraint order was written 4 hours ago and the client remains agitated. The PN should:
options: Continue the restraints indefinitely since the client is still agitated
Follow policy: reassess, ensure the order is still valid/renewed, monitor closely, and report to the RN
Remove the restraints because 4 hours is too long
Tighten the restraints for better control
explain: Correct: B - restraint orders are time-limited and require reassessment, renewal, monitoring, and reporting. A is wrong - restraints cannot continue indefinitely without valid orders. C is wrong - the PN does not unilaterally discontinue; RN/provider direction is needed. D is wrong - restraints must never impair circulation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is diagnosed with influenza. Which precautions should the PN follow? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing a surgical mask when within 3 feet of the client
Placing the client in a private room or cohorting
Wearing an N95 respirator for all routine care
Performing hand hygiene before and after contact
Keeping the door sealed with negative pressure
explain: Correct: A, B, D - influenza requires droplet precautions: surgical mask within 3 feet, private room/cohort, hand hygiene. C and E are wrong - N95 respirators and negative-pressure rooms are for airborne diseases like TB, not droplet-spread influenza.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which precautions are required? Select all that apply.
options: Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
A negative-pressure private room
A surgical mask on the client during transport
A gown and gloves for all routine contact
Keeping the room door closed
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - TB is airborne: N95 for staff, negative-pressure room, mask on the client during transport, door closed. D is wrong - gown and gloves for all routine contact is contact-precaution practice, not required for TB alone.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions are appropriate seizure precautions in the hospital? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the bed in the lowest position
Having suction and oxygen equipment available
Restraining the client's arms at all times
Padding the side rails
Placing a tongue blade at the bedside for use during a seizure
explain: Correct: A, B, D - low bed, suction/oxygen ready, and padded rails protect during a seizure. C is wrong - routine arm restraints are inappropriate and harmful. E is wrong - nothing is ever placed in the mouth during a seizure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing toilet training teaching. Which statement indicates the parent understands readiness?
options: Training should start at exactly 18 months for every child
We will start when our child stays dry for longer periods and shows interest
Punishment speeds up toilet training
Training must be finished before age 2
explain: Correct: B - readiness cues (longer dry periods, interest, communication) guide timing, not the calendar. A and D are wrong - rigid age deadlines ignore developmental variation. C is wrong - punishment causes anxiety and setbacks.

q: The PN reinforces dental health teaching for a young child. Which statement by the parent indicates correct understanding?
options: We will put the baby to bed with a bottle of juice
We will brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and limit sugary drinks
Baby teeth do not matter since they fall out
Dental visits can wait until adulthood
explain: Correct: B - twice-daily fluoride brushing and limiting sugar prevent caries. A is wrong - bedtime juice bottles cause baby-bottle tooth decay. C is wrong - decayed baby teeth affect nutrition, speech, and permanent teeth. D is wrong - early dental visits establish prevention.

q: A pregnant client asks about exercise. The PN reinforces that she should:
options: Avoid all exercise during pregnancy
Continue moderate exercise as approved by her provider, avoiding contact sports and overheating
Begin intense new training to prepare for labor
Exercise only in the third trimester
explain: Correct: B - moderate provider-approved exercise is beneficial; contact sports and overheating are avoided. A is wrong - blanket avoidance is not recommended for uncomplicated pregnancies. C is wrong - starting intense new training is unsafe. D is wrong - there is no third-trimester-only rule.

q: The PN is reinforcing osteoporosis prevention teaching for a postmenopausal client. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will get calcium, vitamin D, do weight-bearing exercise, and avoid smoking
Bed rest is the best way to protect my bones
Only medication can prevent bone loss
High alcohol intake strengthens bones
explain: Correct: A - calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, and not smoking all protect bone density. B is wrong - immobility accelerates bone loss. C is wrong - lifestyle measures are foundational. D is wrong - excess alcohol harms bone.

q: The PN reinforces skin cancer prevention teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I only need sunscreen at the beach in summer
I will use broad-spectrum sunscreen, seek shade midday, and report new or changing moles
A base tan protects me from skin cancer
Tanning beds are safer than sunlight
explain: Correct: B - daily broad-spectrum protection, midday shade, and mole surveillance are the prevention standard. A is wrong - UV exposure is year-round. C is wrong - any tan is skin damage. D is wrong - tanning beds emit concentrated carcinogenic UV.

q: The PN reinforces testicular self-exam teaching for a young adult male. The key point to reinforce is:
options: Exams are only needed after age 60
Perform monthly self-exam and report any lump, swelling, or change to the provider
Self-exam replaces all provider visits
Only athletes need to do this
explain: Correct: B - monthly self-exam with prompt reporting of changes supports early detection. A is wrong - testicular cancer peaks in young men. C is wrong - self-exam supplements, not replaces, care. D is wrong - risk is not limited to athletes.

q: Which health promotion topics should the PN reinforce for a school-age child? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing a helmet when bicycling
Using a seatbelt on every car ride
Avoiding tobacco and alcohol
Skipping meals to stay thin
Playing unsupervised near busy streets
explain: Correct: A, B, C - helmets, seatbelts, and substance avoidance are core school-age safety topics. D is wrong - skipping meals risks disordered eating and poor growth. E is wrong - busy streets are a major injury risk.

q: The PN reinforces healthy-aging teaching for an older adult. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will stay physically active as my provider recommends
I will keep up with recommended vaccines
I will have regular vision and hearing checks
I should accept confusion as a normal part of aging
Isolation is fine as long as I am comfortable
explain: Correct: A, B, C - activity, immunizations, and sensory screening support healthy aging. D is wrong - new confusion is never normal aging and must be evaluated. E is wrong - social isolation harms health; connection matters.

q: A client with a new colostomy says, 'My life is over; nobody will want to be near me.' The PN recognizes this as:
options: A normal reaction that needs no response
Denial, requiring immediate confrontation
An expression of grief and body-image distress needing therapeutic listening and RN notification
A sign the client is ready for discharge
explain: Correct: C - grief and altered body image are expected; the PN listens therapeutically and reports so the RN can arrange support resources. A is wrong - distress should never be ignored. B is wrong - this is grief, not denial, and confrontation is nontherapeutic. D is wrong - emotional distress does not signal discharge readiness.

q: A client who was just diagnosed with diabetes says, 'There is no way I have diabetes; the lab made a mistake.' This is an example of:
options: Projection
Denial
Rationalization
Compensation
explain: Correct: B - denial rejects an unwelcome reality. A is wrong - projection attributes one's own feelings to others. C is wrong - rationalization creates logical excuses, not outright rejection. D is wrong - compensation offsets a weakness with a strength.

q: A client with schizophrenia says, 'The voices are telling me the food is poisoned.' What is the PN's best response?
options: Agree that the food might be poisoned to build trust
State that you do not hear the voices, the food is safe, and encourage eating while notifying the RN
Argue that voices are not real
Remove all food from the room permanently
explain: Correct: B - do not reinforce the hallucination; present reality calmly, encourage nutrition, and report. A is wrong - agreeing validates the delusion. C is wrong - arguing increases agitation without helping. D is wrong - removing all food harms nutrition and does not treat psychosis.

q: The PN is caring for a client in a manic episode. Which approach is best?
options: Provide stimulating group activities to burn energy
Reduce stimuli, offer finger foods, and set firm limits
Engage in lengthy debates about the client's grand plans
Leave the client alone to rest
explain: Correct: B - low stimulation, portable nutrition, and clear limits match manic needs. A is wrong - stimulation worsens mania. C is wrong - debating grandiose ideas is fruitless and escalating. D is wrong - unsupervised manic clients may act impulsively and unsafely.

q: A client is having a panic attack. What should the PN do first?
options: Leave the client alone to calm down
Stay with the client, speak calmly, and guide slow breathing
Tell the client their fear is irrational
Immediately give a PRN sedative without assessment
explain: Correct: B - presence, calm voice, and breathing guidance reduce panic; the PN stays and reports. A is wrong - leaving an acutely panicked client is unsafe. C is wrong - calling fear irrational is judgmental and escalating. D is wrong - medication requires assessment and follows orders, not reflex dosing.

q: A family reports their older parent suddenly became confused and agitated overnight. The PN should recognize this as most consistent with:
options: Normal aging
Delirium, an acute change needing prompt evaluation and RN notification
Dementia, which needs no urgent action
Stubbornness
explain: Correct: B - sudden confusion is delirium until proven otherwise, often from infection, meds, or dehydration, and needs urgent workup. A is wrong - acute confusion is never normal aging. C is wrong - dementia is gradual; sudden change is delirium. D is dismissive and unsafe.

q: Which actions maintain a safe therapeutic milieu on a mental health unit? Select all that apply.
options: Removing or securing objects that could be used for self-harm
Monitoring clients for escalating behavior
Allowing unrestricted access to sharps for independence
Keeping emergency equipment and protocols accessible
Ignoring a client's pacing to avoid confrontation
explain: Correct: A, B, D - environmental safety, behavioral monitoring, and emergency readiness protect everyone. C is wrong - sharps access invites self-harm. E is wrong - pacing can signal escalating agitation that needs early intervention, not ignoring.

q: Which family behaviors are examples of enabling a client with alcohol use disorder? Select all that apply.
options: Bringing alcohol to the client during treatment
Calling the client's employer with excuses to cover absences
Taking over all household duties so the client faces no consequences
Encouraging the client to attend treatment sessions
Setting clear boundaries about alcohol in the home
Lending money the family knows will buy alcohol
explain: Correct: A, B, C, F - supplying alcohol, covering up, shielding from consequences, and funding drinking all enable continued use. D is wrong - encouraging treatment is supportive, not enabling. E is wrong - healthy boundaries oppose enabling.

q: The PN is assisting with range-of-motion exercises for a client on bed rest. The correct technique is:
options: Force joints past the point of pain to maintain flexibility
Move each joint through its full range slowly and gently, stopping if pain occurs
Exercise only the arms since legs matter less
Perform ROM once a week
explain: Correct: B - slow, gentle, full-range movement prevents contractures without injury. A is wrong - forcing past pain tears tissue. C is wrong - all joints need movement. D is wrong - ROM is typically done daily or per orders, not weekly.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing foot care teaching for a client with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Which statement indicates a need for further teaching?
options: I will check my feet daily for cuts or blisters
I will cut my toenails straight across
I can walk barefoot at home since it toughens the skin
I will wear well-fitting shoes and clean socks
explain: Correct: C - barefoot walking risks unnoticed injuries that become infected; this needs correction. A, B, and D all show correct understanding: daily inspection, straight-across nail trimming, and protective footwear.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is providing oral care for an unconscious client. What is the correct technique?
options: Place the client flat and pour water into the mouth
Position the client on the side with head turned, use a swab, and keep suction nearby
Brush aggressively to stimulate consciousness
Skip oral care since the client is not eating
explain: Correct: B - side-lying positioning with suction prevents aspiration during oral care. A is wrong - flat positioning with poured water risks aspiration. C is wrong - aggressive brushing injures tissue and does not restore consciousness. D is wrong - unconscious clients still need oral care to prevent infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN applies a warm compress as ordered. Which safety measure is most important?
options: Leave it on indefinitely for maximum effect
Check the skin frequently and follow the ordered time limit to prevent burns
Apply it directly over an open wound without a barrier
Use the hottest temperature the client can tolerate
explain: Correct: B - heat applications require skin checks and time limits because burns can occur, especially with reduced sensation. A is wrong - indefinite application risks burns. C is wrong - open wounds need sterile technique per orders, not routine compresses. D is wrong - maximum tolerable heat is a burn waiting to happen.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing sleep hygiene teaching for a client with insomnia. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will drink coffee late in the evening to relax
I will keep a regular sleep schedule, limit naps, and avoid caffeine late in the day
I should exercise vigorously right before bed
Watching exciting shows in bed helps me fall asleep
explain: Correct: B - consistent schedule, limited naps, and no late caffeine promote sleep. A is wrong - evening caffeine disrupts sleep. C is wrong - vigorous late exercise is stimulating. D is wrong - exciting screen content delays sleep onset.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client with a hearing aid. Which action is correct?
options: Leave the hearing aid in during an MRI
Remove the hearing aid before the client showers or sleeps, clean it, and store it safely
Share the hearing aid with the roommate who also has hearing loss
Turn the volume to maximum for best hearing
explain: Correct: B - hearing aids are removed for water exposure and sleep, cleaned, and stored safely. A is wrong - electronic devices are unsafe in MRI. C is wrong - hearing aids are fitted to the individual and never shared. D is wrong - maximum volume causes discomfort and feedback.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is providing perineal care for a female client with an indwelling catheter. The correct technique is:
options: Clean from back to front
Clean from front to back, using a clean area of the cloth each stroke
Scrub vigorously with strong soap
Skip perineal care since the catheter keeps the area clean
explain: Correct: B - front-to-back cleaning prevents introducing rectal bacteria to the urethra; fresh cloth areas prevent cross-contamination. A is wrong - back-to-front spreads bacteria toward the urethra. C is wrong - vigorous scrubbing irritates tissue. D is wrong - catheters increase infection risk, making hygiene more important.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help prevent constipation in an immobile client? Select all that apply.
options: Encouraging fluids as permitted
Providing fiber-rich foods as ordered
Encouraging activity as tolerated
Administering prescribed stool softeners
Restricting all fluids to reduce toileting needs
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - fluids, fiber, mobility, and ordered stool softeners all prevent constipation. E is wrong - fluid restriction worsens constipation and risks dehydration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for an incontinent client. Which actions protect skin integrity? Select all that apply.
options: Changing soiled briefs promptly
Cleansing gently and applying barrier cream per orders
Using scented wipes aggressively for odor control
Keeping the skin dry between changes
Leaving the client in a wet brief overnight to promote sleep
explain: Correct: A, B, D - prompt changes, gentle cleansing with barrier protection, and dry skin prevent moisture-associated breakdown. C is wrong - scented products and aggressive wiping irritate skin. E is wrong - prolonged moisture exposure damages skin; sleep never justifies it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which body mechanics should the PN use when moving clients? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the back straight and bending at the knees
Keeping the load close to the body
Twisting at the waist to reposition quickly
Widening the stance for a stable base
Asking for help with heavy or unpredictable clients
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E - straight back, bent knees, close load, wide base, and getting help prevent staff injury. C is wrong - twisting while lifting injures the spine.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes NPH insulin at 8:00 AM. When should the PN be most alert for hypoglycemia?
options: Between 9:00 and 10:00 AM
Between 12:00 PM and 8:00 PM, when NPH peaks
At midnight, 16 hours later
Hypoglycemia cannot occur with NPH
explain: Correct: B - NPH peaks 4 to 12 hours after injection, so midday to evening is the highest hypoglycemia risk window. A is too early for the peak. C is past the typical duration. D is wrong - all insulins can cause hypoglycemia.

q: A diabetic client takes metoprolol. What important teaching should the PN reinforce?
options: Beta blockers prevent all diabetic complications
Beta blockers can mask the warning signs of hypoglycemia, so monitor glucose closely
Metoprolol should be stopped before exercise
Beta blockers increase blood sugar to dangerous levels in everyone
explain: Correct: B - beta blockers blunt sympathetic symptoms like tremor and tachycardia, hiding hypoglycemia; sweating may remain. A is wrong - they do not prevent complications. C is wrong - stopping without orders is unsafe. D overstates - the masking effect is the key issue, not universal severe hyperglycemia.

q: A client takes hydrochlorothiazide. Which finding should the PN report to the RN?
options: Potassium 3.1 mEq/L
Blood pressure 132/84 mmHg
Mild increase in urination
Potassium 4.2 mEq/L
explain: Correct: A - thiazides waste potassium; 3.1 is below the 3.5-5.0 normal range and needs reporting. B is a reasonable BP. C is an expected diuretic effect. D is a normal potassium.

q: A client starting an opioid for post-op pain asks about side effects. The PN should reinforce that the client should:
options: Expect constipation and use fluids, fiber, activity, and ordered laxatives to prevent it
Drive normally since opioids do not affect alertness
Drink alcohol to boost pain relief
Stop the opioid abruptly once pain lessens without telling anyone
explain: Correct: A - constipation is nearly universal with opioids and needs proactive prevention. B is wrong - opioids impair alertness; driving is unsafe. C is wrong - alcohol plus opioids risks fatal respiratory depression. D is wrong - changes to pain management need communication with the team.

q: Naloxone is prescribed for a client receiving opioids. The PN understands its purpose is to:
options: Increase the pain-relieving effect
Reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression in an emergency
Prevent constipation
Treat opioid addiction permanently
explain: Correct: B - naloxone is the opioid antagonist used for overdose with respiratory depression. A is wrong - it blocks, not boosts, opioid effects. C is wrong - it does not treat constipation. D is wrong - it reverses acute overdose; it is not addiction treatment.

q: A male client with benign prostatic hyperplasia is prescribed an antihistamine for allergies. What should the PN monitor and report?
options: Improved allergy symptoms only
Urinary retention, since anticholinergic effects can worsen obstruction
Lower blood pressure
Increased appetite
explain: Correct: B - antihistamines have anticholinergic effects that can precipitate urinary retention in BPH; the PN monitors output and reports difficulty voiding. A ignores the interaction risk. C and D are not the priority concerns with this combination.

q: The PN is reinforcing nitroglycerin teaching for angina. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will sit down, take one dose, and call emergency services if pain is not relieved in 5 minutes
I will take it while driving to the hospital
I will keep the tablets in a clear bottle on the windowsill
Headache and flushing mean I am allergic and should never take it again
explain: Correct: A - sit to prevent syncope, one dose, and emergency help if unrelieved follows standard teaching. B is wrong - driving during angina is unsafe. C is wrong - nitroglycerin degrades in light and must stay in its dark container. D is wrong - headache and flushing are expected vasodilation effects, not allergy.

q: Which findings may indicate digoxin toxicity and must be reported? The PN should watch for:
options: Blurred or yellow-tinged vision, anorexia, nausea, and confusion
Increased appetite and weight gain
Warm, flushed skin
Excessive energy and rapid pulse
explain: Correct: A - visual changes (including yellow-green halos), GI upset, and confusion are classic digoxin toxicity signs. B is wrong - anorexia, not increased appetite, occurs. C is unrelated to digoxin. D is wrong - toxicity more often causes bradycardia and dysrhythmias, not a rapid energetic pulse.

q: A client is starting a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI). Which foods must be avoided? Select all that apply.
options: Aged cheeses
Cured or smoked meats
Red wine and tap beer
Fresh vegetables
Plain rice
explain: Correct: A, B, C - aged, fermented, and cured foods contain tyramine, which with MAOIs can trigger hypertensive crisis. D and E are wrong - fresh vegetables and plain rice are low in tyramine and safe.

q: The PN is reinforcing warfarin teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will keep my intake of vitamin K foods consistent
I will report unusual bleeding, bruising, or blood in urine or stool
I will avoid NSAIDs and excess alcohol
I can start herbal supplements freely since they are natural
I need regular INR blood tests as ordered
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - consistent vitamin K, bleeding surveillance, avoiding NSAIDs/alcohol, and INR monitoring are warfarin essentials. D is wrong - many herbals (ginkgo, garlic, ginseng) interact with warfarin; nothing is added 'freely.'

q: The PN is administering prescribed potassium chloride liquid. Which practices are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Diluting it in water or juice as directed and giving with food
Giving it intravenously by rapid IV push for faster effect
Monitoring for signs of hyperkalemia
Having the client sit upright while drinking it
Giving it on an empty stomach with no fluids
explain: Correct: A, C, D - oral potassium must be diluted to protect the GI tract, taken with food and fluids, upright to prevent irritation, with monitoring for excess. B is wrong - IV push potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest; it is never given that way. E is wrong - undiluted potassium on an empty stomach causes severe GI irritation.

q: A client takes furosemide and gentamicin together. Which finding must the PN report promptly?
options: Mild thirst
New tinnitus or hearing changes
Urine output of 50 mL/hr
Blood pressure 126/78 mmHg
explain: Correct: B - both furosemide and aminoglycosides like gentamicin are ototoxic; combined use raises the risk, and tinnitus or hearing loss needs prompt reporting. A is an expected mild diuretic effect. C is adequate output. D is a normal BP.

q: Before surgery, the PN should ensure the client has:
options: Eaten a full meal for strength
Removed dentures, jewelry, and nail polish, voided, and is wearing only the gown
Applied full makeup to look well
Brought valuables into the operating room
explain: Correct: B - dentures and jewelry are removed for safety, voiding prevents bladder injury and incontinence under anesthesia, and polish interferes with pulse oximetry. A is wrong - pre-op clients are NPO. C is wrong - makeup interferes with skin assessment. D is wrong - valuables are secured, never taken to the OR.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client says something 'gave way' and the PN sees intestines protruding from the incision. What should the PN do?
options: Push the organs back inside and apply pressure
Stay with the client, cover the wound with a sterile saline-moistened dressing, keep the client NPO and still, and call for the RN immediately
Leave to find the surgeon alone
Give the client water to prevent shock
explain: Correct: B - evisceration is an emergency: stay, cover with sterile saline dressing, keep NPO/still with knees slightly bent, and get help at once. A is wrong - never push organs back in. C is wrong - the client must never be left alone. D is wrong - oral intake is contraindicated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is reinforcing post-op leg exercises. The purpose the PN should explain is:
options: To build muscle mass quickly
To promote venous return and help prevent blood clots
To tire the client so they sleep
To replace the need for ambulation
explain: Correct: B - ankle pumps and leg exercises promote venous return, reducing DVT risk. A is wrong - post-op exercises are not for muscle building. C is wrong - fatigue is not the goal. D is wrong - exercises supplement, never replace, early ambulation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client's hemoglobin is 7.2 g/dL (baseline 13.5). The PN should:
options: Document it as normal since the client looks fine
Report it to the RN promptly; the sharp drop suggests bleeding
Encourage the client to eat red meat immediately
Recheck it next week
explain: Correct: B - a hemoglobin drop of this magnitude post-op signals possible hemorrhage and needs urgent evaluation. A is wrong - 7.2 is well below normal (12-16 female, 14-18 male). C is wrong - diet cannot correct acute blood loss. D is wrong - waiting a week with possible bleeding is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest post-op hemorrhage that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Increasingly saturated dressings
Tachycardia with narrowing pulse pressure
Restlessness and cool, pale skin
A single small spot of drainage on the dressing
Stable vital signs matching baseline
explain: Correct: A, B, C - expanding dressing saturation, compensatory tachycardia, and restlessness with pallor are hemorrhage/shock signs. D is wrong - minimal spotting is expected. E is wrong - stable baseline vitals are reassuring, not alarming.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which measures help prevent post-op deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
options: Early ambulation as ordered
Leg exercises and ankle pumps
Sequential compression devices as ordered
Keeping the legs crossed for comfort
Prolonged bed rest without movement
explain: Correct: A, B, C - ambulation, leg exercises, and SCDs all promote venous return. D is wrong - crossed legs impede venous flow. E is wrong - immobility is the primary DVT risk factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which wound findings suggest surgical site infection that the PN should report? Select all that apply.
options: Increasing redness, warmth, and swelling around the incision
Purulent drainage with a foul odor
Fever and increasing incisional pain
A clean, dry, well-approximated incision
Mild itching along a healing incision
explain: Correct: A, B, C - spreading erythema, purulent foul drainage, and fever with worsening pain indicate infection. D is wrong - a clean dry incision is normal healing. E is wrong - mild itching is a common benign healing sensation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client has not voided 8 hours after surgery and reports lower abdominal discomfort. What should the PN do?
options: Wait another 12 hours; this is always normal
Assess for bladder distention, encourage fluids and toileting measures per orders, and report to the RN
Insert an indwelling catheter without an order
Tell the client discomfort is expected and ignore it
explain: Correct: B - 8 hours without voiding post-op suggests retention; the PN assesses, tries ordered measures, and reports. A is wrong - prolonged retention risks bladder injury. C is wrong - catheter insertion requires an order. D is wrong - dismissing the complaint misses a real complication.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's white blood cell count is 18,000/mm3 (normal 4,500-11,000). The PN should:
options: Document it as normal
Recognize possible infection and report it to the RN
Tell the client not to worry since WBCs fight infection
Repeat the test personally in the room
explain: Correct: B - leukocytosis suggests infection or inflammation and needs RN/provider evaluation. A is wrong - 18,000 exceeds the normal range. C is wrong - reassurance without reporting misses the clinical significance. D is wrong - the PN does not run lab tests at the bedside.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A diabetic client's bedtime fingerstick reads 52 mg/dL and the client feels shaky. What should the PN do?
options: Give the bedtime insulin first, then recheck
Follow protocol: give fast-acting carbs, recheck in 15 minutes, and report to the RN
Put the client to bed and recheck in the morning
Give a large high-fat meal
explain: Correct: B - symptomatic hypoglycemia at bedtime needs fast carbs, 15-minute recheck, and RN notification; overnight lows are dangerous. A is wrong - insulin would worsen the low. C is wrong - sleeping through hypoglycemia risks seizure or coma. D is wrong - fat slows glucose absorption; fast carbs come first.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: During an asthma attack, the PN notes audible wheezing and the client cannot complete sentences. What is the PN's priority?
options: Encourage the client to lie flat and relax
Help the client sit upright, administer ordered rescue medication, and notify the RN
Offer a large meal to calm the client
Document the wheezing and reassess in an hour
explain: Correct: B - severe attack with speech limitation needs upright positioning, ordered bronchodilator, and urgent RN notification. A is wrong - flat positioning worsens breathing. C is wrong - eating during an attack risks aspiration. D is wrong - waiting an hour with severe distress is unsafe.

q: An older adult with pneumonia becomes newly confused and restless. The PN should:
options: Assume it is normal aging
Recognize confusion as a sign of hypoxia or worsening infection in older adults and report to the RN immediately
Orient the client once and leave
Restrain the client to prevent wandering
explain: Correct: B - new confusion in an older adult with pneumonia often signals hypoxia or sepsis and needs urgent evaluation. A is wrong - acute confusion is never normal aging. C is wrong - a single orientation attempt does not address the cause. D is wrong - restraints do not treat hypoxia.

q: The PN is reinforcing TB medication teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I can stop the medications once I feel better
I must take the medications for the full 6 to 9 months even when I feel well
One week of medicine cures tuberculosis
I only need medication when I cough
explain: Correct: B - full-course adherence prevents relapse and drug resistance. A is wrong - stopping early causes relapse and resistant TB. C is wrong - TB needs months of therapy. D is wrong - symptoms do not guide treatment duration.

q: A client is diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile. Which hygiene measure should the PN follow and reinforce?
options: Alcohol-based hand sanitizer is sufficient
Handwashing with soap and water, since alcohol does not kill C. difficile spores
No hand hygiene is needed with gloves on
Hand hygiene only before meals
explain: Correct: B - C. difficile forms spores resistant to alcohol sanitizers; soap-and-water washing physically removes them. A is wrong - sanitizer does not kill spores. C is wrong - hand hygiene is still required after glove removal. D is wrong - hygiene is needed before and after every contact.

q: An older adult client has new incontinence, foul-smelling urine, and increased confusion. The PN should suspect:
options: Normal aging changes
A urinary tract infection and report the findings to the RN
Dehydration only, needing no report
Medication side effects that will resolve alone
explain: Correct: B - new incontinence with confusion and urinary changes in older adults classically signals UTI needing evaluation. A is wrong - these are not normal aging. C is wrong - the findings need reporting regardless. D is wrong - assuming self-resolution without assessment is unsafe.

q: The PN is caring for a client with chronic kidney disease. Which finding is most urgent to report?
options: Potassium 6.0 mEq/L
Blood pressure 138/86 mmHg
Mild ankle swelling
A 0.5 kg weight gain since yesterday
explain: Correct: A - hyperkalemia in kidney disease risks fatal dysrhythmia and needs immediate action. B is mildly elevated but not urgent. C and D are fluid-retention signs to monitor and report routinely, but potassium of 6.0 is the emergency.

q: A pregnant client at 34 weeks reports a severe headache, visual spots, and upper abdominal pain. What should the PN do?
options: Reassure her these are normal pregnancy discomforts
Report to the RN immediately; these suggest preeclampsia
Suggest she lie flat on her back
Tell her to wait for her appointment next week
explain: Correct: B - headache, visual changes, and epigastric/RUQ pain are preeclampsia warning signs needing urgent evaluation. A and D are wrong - these are never dismissed as normal. C is wrong - supine positioning can cause vena cava compression; left lateral is preferred.

q: A client with placenta previa begins painless bright-red vaginal bleeding. The PN should:
options: Perform a vaginal exam to assess dilation
Keep the client on bed rest, monitor vitals and bleeding, avoid vaginal exams, and notify the RN immediately
Encourage ambulation to speed labor
Reassure the client that bleeding is expected and needs no report
explain: Correct: B - painless bright-red bleeding suggests placenta previa; vaginal exams can worsen bleeding, so the PN monitors and reports urgently. A is wrong - exams are contraindicated. C is wrong - ambulation is unsafe with active bleeding. D is wrong - this bleeding is an obstetric emergency.

q: The PN assesses a postpartum fundus and finds it boggy and displaced to the right. What should the PN do?
options: Document it as normal
Massage the fundus gently per protocol, assist the client to void, and report to the RN
Apply firm continuous pressure indefinitely
Tell the client to ignore it
explain: Correct: B - a boggy displaced fundus suggests bladder distention preventing contraction; gentle massage, voiding, and RN notification address hemorrhage risk. A is wrong - boggy fundus is not normal. C is wrong - rough prolonged pressure injures tissue. D is wrong - ignoring risks postpartum hemorrhage.

q: The PN is reinforcing newborn thermoregulation teaching. Which parent statement indicates correct understanding?
options: We will bathe the baby in cold water to toughen the skin
We will keep the baby dry, dressed warmly with a hat, and avoid drafts because newborns lose heat quickly
Overheating the room prevents all heat loss
Newborns regulate temperature as well as adults
explain: Correct: B - newborns lose heat rapidly through a large surface area; drying, warm clothing, hats, and draft avoidance prevent cold stress. A is wrong - cold bathing causes dangerous heat loss. C is wrong - overheating risks hyperthermia. D is wrong - newborn thermoregulation is immature.

q: The PN observes a breastfeeding mother. Which observation indicates effective latch that the PN can reinforce positively?
options: Only the nipple tip is in the baby's mouth with clicking sounds
The baby's mouth covers most of the areola with rhythmic sucking and swallowing
The mother reports sharp pain throughout the feeding
The baby falls asleep within 30 seconds without swallowing
explain: Correct: B - wide latch over the areola with rhythmic suck-swallow indicates effective feeding. A is wrong - nipple-only latch with clicking causes pain and poor transfer. C is wrong - persistent sharp pain signals poor latch needing help. D is wrong - no swallowing means no milk transfer.

q: A 2-day-old newborn is increasingly jaundiced with poor feeding. The PN should:
options: Assume jaundice is always normal
Report to the RN promptly; worsening jaundice with poor feeding needs evaluation
Place the baby in direct sunlight on a windowsill
Stop all feedings until the jaundice clears
explain: Correct: B - worsening jaundice with poor feeding can signal significant hyperbilirubinemia needing assessment. A is wrong - not all jaundice is benign. C is wrong - windowsill sunlight is ineffective and risks burns and temperature instability. D is wrong - frequent feeding helps clear bilirubin.

q: A client with appendicitis reports right lower quadrant pain. Which order should the PN question or report as concerning?
options: NPO status
An order for a laxative or enema
IV fluids
Vital signs every 4 hours
explain: Correct: B - laxatives or enemas with appendicitis risk rupture; the PN should clarify/report this order. A is appropriate pre-op preparation. C supports hydration. D is routine monitoring.

q: The PN knows an APGAR score of 8 at 1 minute indicates:
options: Severe distress needing resuscitation
A generally healthy newborn with possibly minor adjustment issues
Fetal death
A score that is never reassessed
explain: Correct: B - APGAR 7-10 indicates good condition; 8 suggests a vigorous newborn with perhaps minor color or tone deductions. A describes scores 0-3. C is wrong - APGAR assesses live newborns. D is wrong - APGAR is repeated at 5 minutes and beyond as needed.

q: Which actions are appropriate when a client is having an asthma exacerbation? Select all that apply.
options: Positioning the client upright
Administering the ordered rescue bronchodilator
Encouraging slow, controlled breathing
Notifying the RN of worsening distress
Encouraging the client to lie flat and breathe into a paper bag
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - upright positioning, ordered bronchodilator, controlled breathing, and RN notification are the correct response. E is wrong - lying flat worsens breathing and paper-bag breathing is for hyperventilation, not asthma.

q: Which findings suggest preeclampsia that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Blood pressure 158/104 mmHg
Severe headache unrelieved by rest
Visual disturbances such as spots or blurring
Protein in the urine
Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - hypertension, severe headache, visual changes, and proteinuria are preeclampsia hallmarks. E is wrong - mild dependent ankle edema can be normal in pregnancy; it is not a preeclampsia criterion alone.

q: Which signs indicate respiratory distress in a newborn that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Nasal flaring
Intercostal retractions
Grunting with expiration
Respiratory rate of 44 breaths/min
Acrocyanosis in the first hours of life
explain: Correct: A, B, C - flaring, retractions, and grunting are distress signs needing immediate reporting. D is wrong - 30-60 breaths/min is the normal newborn range. E is wrong - acrocyanosis (blue hands/feet) is normal in the first day.

q: The PN is reinforcing diet teaching for chronic kidney disease. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will limit sodium, potassium, and phosphorus as instructed
I will follow protein limits set by my provider and dietitian
I will restrict fluids if my provider orders it
I can eat unlimited bananas and oranges for energy
High-sodium processed foods are fine in small amounts daily
explain: Correct: A, B, C - CKD diets limit sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein, and sometimes fluids to reduce kidney workload. D is wrong - bananas and oranges are high-potassium and dangerous in CKD. E is wrong - processed high-sodium foods worsen fluid retention and hypertension.

q: Which precautions should the PN follow for a client with hepatitis B? Select all that apply.
options: Standard precautions for blood and body fluids
Advising the client not to share razors, toothbrushes, or needles
Wearing a respirator mask for all routine care
Double-bagging all linens as infectious waste
Reinforcing the importance of household contacts discussing vaccination with their provider
explain: Correct: A, B, E - hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids: standard precautions, no sharing of blood-contaminated items, and vaccination discussion for contacts. C is wrong - hepatitis B is not airborne; no respirator is needed. D is wrong - routine linen handling with standard precautions suffices.

q: The PN is reinforcing GERD teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating
I will eat smaller, more frequent meals
I will avoid tobacco and excess alcohol
I should eat large spicy meals before bed
Tight belts and waistbands are fine
explain: Correct: A, B, C - staying upright after meals, smaller meals, and avoiding tobacco/alcohol reduce reflux. D is wrong - large spicy late meals worsen GERD. E is wrong - tight abdominal pressure promotes reflux.

q: Which findings suggest bowel obstruction that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Crampy abdominal pain with distention
Vomiting with inability to pass flatus
High-pitched bowel sounds early, then absent sounds
Soft, nondistended abdomen with normal bowel movements
Increasing abdominal girth measurements
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - crampy pain, distention, vomiting without flatus, hyperactive-then-absent bowel sounds, and increasing girth all signal obstruction. D is wrong - a soft abdomen with normal stools contradicts obstruction.

q: Which are risk factors for postpartum hemorrhage that the PN should monitor for? Select all that apply.
options: Prolonged or rapid labor
Multiple gestation
Large baby (macrosomia)
A firm, contracted fundus
Retained placental fragments
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - prolonged/precipitate labor, multiples, macrosomia, and retained fragments all predispose to uterine atony and hemorrhage. D is wrong - a firm contracted fundus is protective, not a risk factor.

q: A client insists on leaving the hospital against medical advice (AMA). What is the PN's best action?
options: Physically prevent the client from leaving
Notify the RN and provider, document the client's statements and actions objectively, and reinforce the risks of leaving as the RN directs
Have security remove the client's belongings
Sign the AMA form on the client's behalf
explain: Correct: B - competent clients may leave AMA; the PN notifies the team, documents objectively, and reinforces risks without coercion. A is wrong - physically detaining a competent client is false imprisonment. C is wrong - security is not needed for a competent adult leaving. D is wrong - the client signs their own AMA form; the PN may witness.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is documenting a client's pain reassessment after medication. The most important elements to include are:
options: The PN's guess about why the client has pain
The pain rating, what was done, and the client's response to the intervention
Only the medication name
A note that the client 'tolerated it well' with no details
explain: Correct: B - pain reassessment documentation needs the rating, intervention, and response to show effectiveness. A is wrong - guesses do not belong in the record. C is wrong - the name alone shows nothing about outcome. D is wrong - vague phrases without data are poor documentation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client's potassium result of 6.1 mEq/L appears in the chart. The PN should:
options: File the result and mention it at the next shift huddle
Report the critical value to the RN immediately per policy
Recheck it with a different lab machine personally
Wait for the provider to notice it
explain: Correct: B - critical lab values require immediate reporting per policy; hyperkalemia can be lethal. A is wrong - waiting for a huddle delays urgent treatment. C is wrong - the PN does not rerun lab analyzers. D is wrong - the PN is responsible for communicating critical results, not waiting.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN believes a provider's order is unsafe for the client. What is the correct sequence?
options: Carry it out and document disagreement
Clarify with the provider; if unresolved, escalate through the chain of command and do not carry out an unsafe order
Ask the UAP to carry it out instead
Change the order to what seems safer
explain: Correct: B - the PN clarifies first, then escalates; an unsafe order is never carried out. A is wrong - carrying out a known unsafe order violates the duty to protect. C is wrong - delegating does not transfer accountability. D is wrong - the PN cannot rewrite provider orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family member asks the PN for details about another client's condition. The PN should:
options: Share the information since the families know each other
Decline politely, explaining that client information is confidential
Share only the diagnosis but not the treatment
Ask the other client for permission first, then share freely
explain: Correct: B - confidentiality applies to everyone; the PN declines politely. A is wrong - acquaintance does not authorize disclosure. C is wrong - partial disclosure is still a violation. D is wrong - putting the client on the spot is inappropriate; the default is non-disclosure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is contributing to a client's care plan. Which contribution is appropriate?
options: Writing the nursing diagnoses independently
Providing collected data such as vital sign trends and the client's reported symptoms
Setting the discharge date
Ordering diagnostic tests
explain: Correct: B - the PN contributes data; the RN synthesizes it into diagnoses and plans. A is wrong - nursing diagnosis is the RN's role. C is wrong - discharge timing is a provider/team decision. D is wrong - the PN does not order diagnostics.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client expresses interest in organ donation. The PN's best action is to:
options: Talk the client out of it
Acknowledge the interest, document it, and report it to the RN so proper resources are provided
Complete the donor paperwork independently
Ignore the comment as unrelated to nursing care
explain: Correct: B - the PN supports the expressed wish, documents, and refers to the RN for the formal process. A is wrong - discouraging donation imposes the PN's values. C is wrong - formal consent processes involve designated staff. D is wrong - the wish deserves a response and referral.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN almost administers the wrong dose but catches the error before giving it. What should the PN do?
options: Say nothing since no harm occurred
Report the near miss per facility policy so systems can be improved
Only tell the client
Document that the medication was given
explain: Correct: B - near-miss reporting drives system improvement and is protected quality activity. A is wrong - silence wastes a learning opportunity. C is wrong - telling only the client does not fix the system. D is wrong - documenting a false administration is fraud.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which action by the PN best demonstrates cost-effective care?
options: Opening extra supply kits just in case
Using only the supplies needed, avoiding waste, and reporting malfunctioning equipment
Skipping ordered treatments to save money
Reusing single-use items between clients
explain: Correct: B - stewardship means using what is needed without waste. A is wrong - 'just in case' waste raises costs. C is wrong - skipping ordered care harms clients and is not stewardship. D is wrong - reusing single-use items spreads infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The RN delegates tracheostomy suctioning for a client with an established trach to the experienced PN. This is appropriate because:
options: Suctioning an established tracheostomy is within PN scope when competency is verified
The RN is too busy
UAPs refused to do it
Tracheostomies never need suctioning
explain: Correct: A - suctioning an established trach is a standard PN skill once competency is confirmed. B is wrong - busyness does not justify delegation; scope and competence do. C is wrong - UAP refusal is irrelevant to scope. D is factually wrong.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client refuses a bath. The PN's best response is to:
options: Insist the bath is required and proceed anyway
Respect the refusal, explore the reason, offer alternatives, and document
Have the UAP do it while the client sleeps
Skip hygiene for the rest of the hospitalization
explain: Correct: B - clients may refuse care; the PN respects autonomy, problem-solves, and documents. A is wrong - forcing care violates autonomy and can be battery. C is wrong - doing it during sleep is deceptive. D is wrong - one refusal does not end all future hygiene offers.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is caring for a client in isolation for a contagious illness. The client's family is upset about visiting restrictions. The PN should:
options: Let the family visit without precautions to keep them happy
Explain the reasons for precautions empathetically and reinforce the teaching about safe visiting
Ban the family from the unit
Ignore the family's concerns
explain: Correct: B - empathetic explanation plus reinforced teaching balances safety and family needs. A is wrong - waiving precautions endangers everyone. C is wrong - banning family is unnecessarily harsh. D is wrong - ignoring concerns damages trust.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A new PN asks what 'standard of care' means. The best explanation is:
options: Whatever the most senior nurse prefers
The level of care a reasonably prudent nurse with similar training would provide in similar circumstances
The minimum needed to avoid complaints
Whatever the client requests
explain: Correct: B - standard of care is the legal benchmark of prudent practice. A is wrong - seniority does not define the standard. C is wrong - complaint-avoidance is not the measure. D is wrong - client requests do not override professional standards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to witness a client's advance directive. The PN should verify that the client:
options: Has already decided without any discussion
Appears to understand the document, is signing voluntarily, and has had questions answered by the appropriate person
Is over 65 years old
Has a terminal diagnosis
explain: Correct: B - witnessing confirms apparent understanding and voluntariness after questions were addressed. A is wrong - some discussion is expected; the witness confirms it happened appropriately. C is wrong - age is not the criterion; competence is. D is wrong - advance directives are for any competent adult.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which tasks can the PN appropriately delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.
options: Ambulating a stable client
Collecting a urine specimen
Changing bed linens for a stable client
Assessing lung sounds
Deciding which clients need pain medication
explain: Correct: A, B, C - ambulation, specimen collection, and linen changes for stable clients are routine delegable tasks. D is wrong - assessment requires nursing judgment. E is wrong - medication decisions are never delegated to UAPs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is preparing an end-of-shift report. Which items must be included? Select all that apply.
options: Abnormal vital signs and the actions taken
Pending labs, procedures, or consults
Fall risk status and safety precautions in place
The PN's personal opinions about the provider
New orders received during the shift
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - abnormal vitals with actions, pending items, safety status, and new orders ensure continuity. D is wrong - personal opinions about providers are unprofessional and irrelevant to handoff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions by the PN support continuity of care? Select all that apply.
options: Documenting care promptly and accurately
Communicating changes in condition to the RN
Following the established care plan
Making independent changes to the care plan without telling anyone
Reviewing the chart before providing care
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - timely documentation, change communication, plan adherence, and chart review all support continuity. D is wrong - silent independent changes fragment care and are outside PN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with diabetes is NPO for surgery and the RN is titrating insulin per protocol. The PN's appropriate roles include: Select all that apply.
options: Monitoring for signs of hypoglycemia
Checking fingerstick glucose as ordered
Reporting abnormal glucose results to the RN promptly
Independently deciding the insulin dose
Offering the client juice while NPO
explain: Correct: A, B, C - monitoring, ordered glucose checks, and prompt reporting are PN roles. D is wrong - titration decisions belong to the RN per protocol. E is wrong - giving juice violates NPO status.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements reflect correct understanding of the PN's accountability? Select all that apply.
options: The PN is accountable for tasks performed, including those delegated to UAPs
The PN must practice within the scope defined by the state nurse practice act
The PN can be held liable for carrying out a known unsafe order
Accountability ends when the shift ends
Only the RN is accountable for anything that happens on the unit
explain: Correct: A, B, C - accountability follows the PN's own actions and delegations, is bounded by the practice act, and includes refusing unsafe orders. D is wrong - documentation and handoff extend responsibility beyond clock-out. E is wrong - every licensed nurse is accountable for their own practice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Before administering any medication, the PN must verify the client's identity using:
options: The room number
Two identifiers such as name and date of birth, checked against the armband
Recognition of the client's face alone
Asking the roommate to confirm
explain: Correct: B - two identifiers (name, DOB) matched to the armband and order is the safety standard. A is wrong - room numbers change and are not identifiers. C is wrong - familiarity is not a substitute for identifier checks. D is wrong - roommates cannot verify identity.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN notes a client's allergy band lists penicillin, but the MAR shows a newly ordered penicillin-type antibiotic. What should the PN do?
options: Give the first dose and watch for a reaction
Hold the medication and report the discrepancy to the RN immediately
Remove the allergy band since it may be outdated
Give a smaller test dose
explain: Correct: B - an allergy-band versus order mismatch is a critical safety stop; the PN holds and reports. A is wrong - administering risks anaphylaxis. C is wrong - the PN never removes allergy identification. D is wrong - 'test doses' of allergens are dangerous and outside scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client at risk for suicide is admitted. Which environmental safety measures should the PN ensure?
options: Leaving sharps and cords within reach to promote independence
Removing harmful objects, checking the room for hazards, and following observation protocols
Allowing the client to keep all personal items uninspected
Placing the client in a remote room with no observation
explain: Correct: B - ligature and sharps removal plus prescribed observation levels protect the client. A is wrong - accessible sharps and cords enable self-harm. C is wrong - personal items must be screened per protocol. D is wrong - isolation without observation is the opposite of safe care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing home oxygen safety teaching. Which statement indicates the client needs further teaching?
options: I will not smoke while using oxygen
I can use petroleum jelly on my nose to prevent dryness
I will keep oxygen away from open flames
I will not adjust the flow rate without direction
explain: Correct: B - petroleum products near oxygen are a fire hazard; water-based products should be used. A, C, and D all show correct understanding: no smoking, no flames, and no unsupervised flow changes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A toddler is brought to the clinic after swallowing an unknown pill. The PN's first action is to:
options: Induce vomiting immediately
Call poison control and report the child's age, weight, substance if known, and symptoms
Give milk to dilute the pill
Wait for symptoms before acting
explain: Correct: B - poison control gives substance-specific guidance; the PN gathers key data first. A is wrong - vomiting is not always indicated and can cause harm. C is wrong - milk is not a universal antidote. D is wrong - waiting wastes the early treatment window.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing car seat teaching for an infant. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: The infant should ride in a rear-facing seat in the back seat
The infant can ride in the front seat if held by an adult
A forward-facing seat is safest for newborns
Car seats are only needed for long trips
explain: Correct: A - rear-facing in the back seat is the standard for infants. B is wrong - holding a baby is never a substitute for a car seat, and the front seat risks airbag injury. C is wrong - newborns must be rear-facing. D is wrong - restraints are needed on every ride.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A confused client keeps trying to leave the unit. Which is the best initial action?
options: Apply restraints immediately
Redirect and engage the client, ensure supervision, notify the RN, and consider elopement precautions per policy
Let the client leave since they want to go
Lock the client in the room alone
explain: Correct: B - redirection, supervision, RN notification, and policy-based elopement precautions are the least restrictive safe response. A is wrong - restraints are a last resort with an order. C is wrong - an unsafe confused client must not wander off. D is wrong - locking a client in a room alone is unsafe and inappropriate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN finds a client on the floor. After assessing for injury and notifying the RN, the PN should first:
options: Help the client up immediately to reduce embarrassment
Keep the client still until assessed, then assist safely per the RN's direction
Tell the client to get up alone
Move the client to a chair quickly
explain: Correct: B - a fallen client is kept still until injury is assessed to avoid worsening harm, then moved safely. A is wrong - rushing the client up risks spinal or fracture injury. C is wrong - an injured client should not get up alone. D is wrong - quick moves before assessment are unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which situation is a 'near miss' that the PN should report?
options: A medication error that reached the client and caused harm
A wrong dose drawn up but caught and corrected before administration
A client complimenting the staff
A routine vital sign within normal limits
explain: Correct: B - a caught-before-harm error is the classic near miss; reporting it improves systems. A is an actual adverse event, not a near miss. C and D are not safety events at all.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions reduce the risk of health care-associated infections? Select all that apply.
options: Performing hand hygiene between clients
Disinfecting shared equipment between uses
Wearing the same gown for all clients on the unit
Following isolation precautions as posted
Leaving urinary catheters in place for convenience
explain: Correct: A, B, D - hand hygiene, equipment disinfection, and isolation compliance prevent transmission. C is wrong - gowns are single-client use. E is wrong - catheters are removed as soon as unneeded to prevent CAUTI.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is caring for a client with varicella (chickenpox). Which precautions apply? Select all that apply.
options: Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
Contact precautions for skin lesions
A negative-pressure room if available
A surgical mask for routine entry
Placing the client with a roommate who never had chickenpox
explain: Correct: A, B, C - varicella is airborne plus contact: N95, contact precautions for lesions, negative-pressure room. D is wrong - a surgical mask does not protect against airborne virus. E is wrong - a nonimmune roommate would be exposed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are correct steps for donning personal protective equipment? Select all that apply.
options: Performing hand hygiene before donning
Putting on the gown first, then mask, then eye protection, then gloves
Securing the mask snugly over nose and mouth
Putting gloves on over the gown cuffs
Donning PPE in the hallway after entering the room
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - hand hygiene first, then gown, mask, eye protection, gloves over cuffs, with a snug mask seal. E is wrong - PPE is donned before entering the isolation room, not after.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about colon cancer screening. The PN should reinforce that screening generally begins at age:
options: 25 for everyone
45 for average-risk adults, or earlier if high risk
65 regardless of history
Only when symptoms appear
explain: Correct: B - average-risk screening starts at 45; high-risk clients start earlier per provider. A is too early for average risk. C misses the recommended start age. D defeats the purpose of screening, which finds disease before symptoms.

q: A parent asks when a child should first see a dentist. The PN reinforces:
options: By the first birthday or when the first tooth appears
Only when there is tooth pain
At age 10
Dental visits are unnecessary for children
explain: Correct: A - first dental visit by age 1 or first tooth establishes prevention early. B is wrong - waiting for pain means decay is advanced. C is far too late. D is wrong - children need dental care.

q: The PN reinforces shingles vaccine teaching for a 60-year-old. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: The vaccine is only for people who never had chickenpox
The recombinant shingles vaccine is recommended for adults 50 and older
One shingles episode means I never need the vaccine
Antibiotics prevent shingles
explain: Correct: B - shingles vaccine is recommended at 50+ even after prior shingles or chickenpox. A is wrong - prior chickenpox is the reason vaccination matters. C is wrong - recurrence is possible, so vaccination is still recommended. D is wrong - shingles is viral; antibiotics do not prevent it.

q: An older adult asks how to stay strong and prevent falls. The PN reinforces:
options: Complete bed rest to avoid injury
Regular provider-approved exercise including balance and strength activities
Avoiding all physical activity after 70
Only exercising when feeling unsteady
explain: Correct: B - balance and strength exercise reduce fall risk. A is wrong - bed rest weakens muscles and bones. C is wrong - inactivity accelerates decline. D is wrong - exercising only when unsteady is reactive, not preventive.

q: The PN is reinforcing HPV vaccine teaching for the parent of an 11-year-old. The key point is:
options: The vaccine is only for adults
Routine HPV vaccination is recommended starting at ages 11-12 to prevent HPV-related cancers
The vaccine treats existing infections
One dose in childhood is never followed by anything else
explain: Correct: B - routine HPV vaccination at 11-12 prevents cancer-causing HPV types. A is wrong - the target age is preteen. C is wrong - the vaccine is preventive, not therapeutic. D is wrong - the series involves multiple doses per schedule.

q: A pregnant client asks whether dental cleanings are safe during pregnancy. The PN reinforces that:
options: All dental care must be avoided until after delivery
Routine dental care, including cleanings, is safe and important during pregnancy
Gum disease has no effect on pregnancy outcomes
Dental X-rays are required at every prenatal visit
explain: Correct: B - routine dental care is safe in pregnancy, and periodontal disease is associated with preterm birth, so care should not be postponed. A is wrong - avoiding all care allows disease to progress. C is wrong - gum disease is linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes. D is wrong - routine dental X-rays are not a prenatal requirement.

q: Which immunizations should the PN reinforce for adults 65 and older? Select all that apply.
options: Annual influenza vaccine
Pneumococcal vaccine as recommended
Shingles (recombinant zoster) vaccine
The full childhood vaccine series repeated yearly
HPV vaccine as a first dose at 70
explain: Correct: A, B, C - flu, pneumococcal, and shingles vaccines are recommended for older adults. D is wrong - childhood series are not repeated yearly. E is wrong - HPV vaccination is targeted to younger ages, not initiated at 70.

q: The PN reinforces injury prevention for an adolescent. Which topics are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Seatbelt use on every ride
Avoiding alcohol and drugs, especially with driving
Wearing helmets for bikes and sports
Trying risky dares to fit in
Texting while driving if experienced
explain: Correct: A, B, C - seatbelts, substance avoidance, and helmets prevent the leading causes of teen injury and death. D is wrong - dares risk serious injury. E is wrong - texting while driving is dangerous regardless of experience.

q: A client says, 'I do not need my antidepressant anymore; I feel fine.' What is the PN's best response?
options: Agree and tell the client to stop the medication
Encourage the client to discuss it with the provider before making changes and report the statement to the RN
Tell the client they will be depressed forever
Hide the medication so the client cannot stop it
explain: Correct: B - feeling better often means the drug is working; changes need provider direction, and the RN must know. A is wrong - the PN never advises stopping. C is wrong - hopeless predictions are nontherapeutic. D is wrong - deception violates trust and autonomy.

q: A client with anorexia nervosa is admitted. The PN's priority in the milieu is to:
options: Comment on the client's appearance to motivate eating
Monitor meals and eating behaviors per the plan, provide a structured supportive environment, and report concerns to the RN
Allow the client to skip all meals to avoid conflict
Weigh the client openly in front of peers
explain: Correct: B - structured monitoring with therapeutic support and RN reporting is the PN's role. A is wrong - appearance comments worsen body image. C is wrong - allowing meal-skipping enables the disorder. D is wrong - public weigh-ins are shaming and nontherapeutic.

q: A client in alcohol withdrawal is tremulous and anxious 12 hours after the last drink. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client that withdrawal is harmless
Keep the client safe, monitor vital signs, and report to the RN immediately since withdrawal can progress to seizures
Give the client a drink to calm the tremors
Leave the client alone to rest
explain: Correct: B - alcohol withdrawal can escalate to seizures and delirium tremens; close monitoring and RN notification are essential. A is wrong - withdrawal can be life-threatening. C is wrong - giving alcohol is never therapeutic. D is wrong - the client needs observation, not isolation.

q: A client who lost a spouse 2 months ago says, 'I keep expecting him to walk through the door.' The PN recognizes this as:
options: Abnormal prolonged grief requiring confrontation
A normal early grief response; the PN listens supportively and reports concerns per the plan
Denial that must be broken through immediately
A sign of psychosis
explain: Correct: B - sensing the deceased's presence is a common normal grief experience; supportive listening is therapeutic. A is wrong - 2 months is early grief, not prolonged disorder. C is wrong - grief is not 'broken through' by confrontation. D is wrong - this is not psychosis.

q: A client discloses intimate partner violence and asks the PN not to tell anyone. The PN's best action is to:
options: Promise absolute secrecy
Explain limits of confidentiality, ensure immediate safety, and report per facility policy and law
Tell the client to go home and work it out
Confront the partner in the waiting room
explain: Correct: B - safety comes first; the PN cannot promise secrecy about abuse and must follow reporting laws and policy. A is wrong - promising secrecy the PN cannot keep destroys trust. C is wrong - sending the client back without resources endangers them. D is wrong - confronting the partner risks escalation and is unsafe.

q: A client with dementia becomes agitated at sundown. The PN's best initial approach is to:
options: Argue with the client about the time of day
Use a calm routine, reduce noise and shadows, redirect gently, and report patterns to the RN
Restrain the client until morning
Give a sedative without an order
explain: Correct: B - sundowning responds to calm routines, environmental tweaks, and redirection; patterns are reported for plan adjustment. A is wrong - arguing with dementia increases agitation. C is wrong - restraints are a last resort. D is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope.

q: Which responses are therapeutic when a client expresses hopelessness? Select all that apply.
options: You seem to be feeling hopeless right now
Tell me what is going through your mind
I will stay with you for a while
Cheer up; things are not that bad
I know exactly how you feel
explain: Correct: A, B, C - reflecting feelings, open-ended exploration, and therapeutic presence are appropriate for hopelessness. D is wrong - minimizing dismisses the client's pain. E is wrong - the PN cannot know exactly how the client feels.

q: Which behaviors suggest a client may be experiencing a crisis needing urgent RN notification? Select all that apply.
options: Stating a plan to harm self or others
Giving away prized possessions suddenly
Extreme agitation with threatening behavior
Calmly reading a book
Requesting an extra blanket
explain: Correct: A, B, C - stated harm plans, giving away possessions, and threatening agitation are crisis indicators. D and E are ordinary comfort behaviors needing no urgent action.

q: The PN is teaching a client to use a cane. The correct instruction is:
options: Hold the cane on the weak side
Hold the cane on the strong side and move the cane with the weak leg
Hold the cane in the middle with both hands
The cane height does not matter
explain: Correct: B - the cane goes on the strong side and advances with the weak leg for support. A is wrong - weak-side placement provides no support where needed. C is wrong - one-handed use on the strong side is correct. D is wrong - proper height (wrist crease level) prevents poor posture and falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for dentures. The correct procedure is:
options: Clean them over a sink full of water or a towel, using a brush and denture cleaner
Use hot water to sterilize them
Store them dry in a tissue
Let the client sleep with them always without cleaning
explain: Correct: A - cleaning over water or a towel prevents breakage if dropped. B is wrong - hot water warps dentures. C is wrong - they should be stored in water or solution, labeled. D is wrong - dentures need daily cleaning and gums need rest.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with dyspnea is most comfortable in which position?
options: Flat on the back
High Fowler's or sitting upright leaning slightly forward
Trendelenburg
Prone without support
explain: Correct: B - upright positioning lets the diaphragm descend and expands lung capacity. A is wrong - flat positioning worsens dyspnea. C is wrong - Trendelenburg pushes abdominal contents against the diaphragm. D is wrong - unsupported prone restricts breathing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing Kegel exercise teaching for urinary incontinence. The correct instruction is:
options: Bear down like having a bowel movement
Tighten the pelvic floor muscles as if stopping urine flow, hold, then relax, repeating several times daily
Hold the breath during the exercises
Do Kegels only once a month
explain: Correct: B - Kegels strengthen pelvic floor muscles through repeated contraction and relaxation. A is wrong - bearing down strains rather than strengthens. C is wrong - breath-holding raises intra-abdominal pressure. D is wrong - benefits require regular daily practice.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a client with a walker. The correct technique is to:
options: Push the walker far ahead and step into it
Move the walker a short distance forward, then step into it while standing upright
Pull the walker behind while walking
Lean heavily over the walker with a hunched back
explain: Correct: B - short forward moves with upright posture keep the walker stable and the client balanced. A is wrong - pushing it far ahead causes overreaching and falls. C is wrong - a walker behind provides no support. D is wrong - hunching impairs balance and breathing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A post-op client needs to cough and deep breathe. The PN should instruct the client to:
options: Cough without any support to build strength
Splint the incision with a pillow, breathe deeply, and cough firmly
Avoid coughing to protect the incision
Take rapid shallow breaths only
