explain: Correct: B - splinting supports the incision while effective coughing clears secretions. A is wrong - unsupported coughing is painful and clients will avoid it. C is wrong - suppressing coughs invites atelectasis. D is wrong - shallow breaths do not expand alveoli.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client reports nausea after surgery. Which PN action is best?
options: Offer a large meal to settle the stomach
Provide small sips of clear fluids as ordered, reduce odors, and report persistent nausea to the RN
Encourage the client to lie flat immediately after eating
Give an antiemetic without an order
explain: Correct: B - small sips, odor control, and reporting follow post-op nausea management within PN scope. A is wrong - large meals worsen nausea. C is wrong - lying flat after intake increases aspiration risk with nausea. D is wrong - medication requires an order.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures promote regular bowel function in a hospitalized client? Select all that apply.
options: Encouraging fluids and fiber as ordered
Promoting activity as tolerated
Providing privacy and unhurried time for toileting
Administering prescribed bowel regimen medications
Encouraging the client to ignore the urge to defecate
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - fluids, fiber, mobility, privacy, and ordered bowel medications all support regularity. E is wrong - ignoring the urge leads to constipation and impaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a dyspneic client. Which comfort measures are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Positioning upright in high Fowler's
Administering oxygen as ordered
Keeping the environment calm and uncluttered
Encouraging slow, pursed-lip breathing
Placing the client flat with legs elevated
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - upright positioning, ordered oxygen, calm environment, and pursed-lip breathing ease dyspnea. E is wrong - flat positioning worsens breathing difficulty.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which home safety measures help prevent falls in older adults? Select all that apply.
options: Removing throw rugs and clutter from walkways
Installing grab bars in the bathroom
Improving lighting, especially at night
Wearing sturdy, nonskid footwear
Waxing floors to a high shine
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - clear walkways, grab bars, good lighting, and safe footwear prevent falls. E is wrong - highly waxed floors are slippery and dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is teaching a client to mix NPH and regular insulin. The correct order is:
options: Draw up the cloudy NPH first, then the clear regular
Draw up the clear regular first, then the cloudy NPH
Shake the vial vigorously before drawing up
Mixing insulins is never done
explain: Correct: B - 'clear before cloudy' prevents contaminating the regular insulin with NPH. A reverses the order and risks contamination. C is wrong - insulin is rolled gently, never shaken. D is wrong - NPH and regular are routinely mixed.

q: A client takes levothyroxine. The PN reinforces that it should be taken:
options: At bedtime with a large meal
In the morning on an empty stomach, separate from calcium and iron
Only when feeling tired
With antacids to prevent stomach upset
explain: Correct: B - morning empty-stomach dosing maximizes absorption; calcium and iron bind the drug. A is wrong - food reduces absorption. C is wrong - it is daily therapy, not as-needed. D is wrong - antacids impair absorption.

q: A client asks why prednisone cannot be stopped suddenly. The PN's best explanation is:
options: Stopping suddenly is fine if you feel better
The body reduces its own steroid production during therapy, so the dose must be tapered as ordered to avoid adrenal crisis
Tapering is only needed for injections
Sudden stopping improves immunity
explain: Correct: B - prolonged steroids suppress the adrenal axis; tapering lets it recover. A is wrong - abrupt stop risks adrenal crisis. C is wrong - tapering applies to oral steroids too. D is wrong - the opposite is true.

q: The PN is reinforcing NSAID teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will take it on an empty stomach for faster relief
I will take it with food or milk and report stomach pain or black stools
I can safely double the dose if pain is severe
NSAIDs have no effect on the stomach
explain: Correct: B - food protects the stomach lining, and pain or melena signals GI bleeding to report. A is wrong - empty-stomach NSAIDs irritate the mucosa. C is wrong - exceeding the dose raises bleeding and kidney risks. D is wrong - GI irritation and bleeding are major NSAID risks.

q: A client takes acetaminophen regularly for arthritis. What is the most important teaching point the PN should reinforce?
options: Acetaminophen is completely safe at any dose
Do not exceed the maximum daily dose (generally 3,000-4,000 mg) because overdose causes liver damage, and check combination products for hidden acetaminophen
Take it with alcohol to increase effect
It reduces inflammation like ibuprofen
explain: Correct: B - liver toxicity is the critical risk, and many combination products hide acetaminophen. A is wrong - no drug is safe at any dose. C is wrong - alcohol plus acetaminophen greatly increases liver injury. D is wrong - acetaminophen is not an anti-inflammatory.

q: A client taking diphenhydramine for allergies drives for a living. What should the PN reinforce?
options: It never causes drowsiness
It can cause significant drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until the effects are known
Take extra doses before driving to stay alert
Drowsiness means the drug is not working
explain: Correct: B - first-generation antihistamines sedate; driving and alcohol are unsafe until response is known. A is wrong - drowsiness is common. C is wrong - extra doses worsen sedation. D is wrong - sedation is a side effect, not a sign of failure.

q: A client with hypertension asks about over-the-counter pseudoephedrine for congestion. The PN should:
options: Recommend it as completely safe
Advise the client to check with the provider or pharmacist first, since decongestants can raise blood pressure
Tell the client to double the blood pressure medication that day
Say nothing; it is the client's choice
explain: Correct: B - decongestants can elevate BP and interact with antihypertensives; provider/pharmacist guidance is needed. A is wrong - it is not risk-free in hypertension. C is wrong - the PN never advises dose changes. D is wrong - the PN has a duty to share safety information.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client starting an antihypertensive. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will rise slowly from sitting or lying to prevent dizziness
I will stop the medication once my pressure is normal
I can drink heavily on weekends
Dizziness when standing is a sign the drug is curing me
explain: Correct: A - rising slowly counters orthostatic hypotension. B is wrong - stopping without direction risks rebound hypertension. C is wrong - heavy alcohol raises BP and interacts with the drug. D is wrong - orthostatic dizziness is a side effect to manage and report, not a cure sign.

q: The PN is reinforcing antibiotic teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will take the full course even if I feel better
I will report rash, itching, or difficulty breathing immediately
I will take it with a full glass of water as directed
I can share leftover antibiotics with family members
I should stop the antibiotic if I develop severe watery diarrhea and call the provider
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - full course prevents resistance, allergic signs need immediate reporting, proper administration matters, and severe diarrhea may signal C. difficile needing provider direction. D is wrong - antibiotics are never shared; different infections need different drugs.

q: Which are correct practices for safe medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Checking the order against the MAR using the five rights
Verifying client identity with two identifiers
Checking the expiration date
Administering a medication another nurse prepared without verifying it
Documenting administration promptly after giving it
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - five rights, two identifiers, expiry checks, and prompt documentation are safety fundamentals. D is wrong - the administering nurse verifies every medication personally.

q: The PN is caring for a client receiving IV potassium. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Verifying the infusion rate against the order and pump settings
Monitoring the IV site for irritation or infiltration
Reporting signs of hyperkalemia such as muscle weakness or ECG changes
Giving the IV potassium by rapid bolus if the level is very low
Assessing cardiac rhythm per protocol
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - rate verification, site monitoring, hyperkalemia surveillance, and rhythm assessment are essential with IV potassium. D is wrong - IV push potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest; it is infused at controlled rates only.

q: The order is for 2 g of a medication; available: 500 mg tablets. How many tablets should the PN administer?
options: 0.5 tablet
2 tablets
4 tablets
8 tablets
explain: Correct: C - convert grams to milligrams first: 2 g = 2000 mg; 2000 mg divided by 500 mg per tablet = 4 tablets. A gives 250 mg. B gives 1000 mg, half the dose. D gives 4000 mg, double the dose.

q: Before a thoracentesis, the PN positions the client:
options: Flat on the back
Sitting upright leaning forward over a bedside table
Lying on the affected side
In Trendelenburg
explain: Correct: B - sitting and leaning forward spreads the ribs and exposes the pleural space. A is wrong - supine does not open the intercostal spaces. C is wrong - lying on the affected side compresses it. D is wrong - Trendelenburg is unrelated to thoracentesis positioning.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a paracentesis, the PN should ensure the client has:
options: Eaten a full meal
Voided to empty the bladder and reduce injury risk
Drunk a large amount of water
Removed all clothing permanently
explain: Correct: B - an empty bladder reduces the risk of bladder puncture during paracentesis. A is wrong - clients are typically NPO or lightly restricted. C is wrong - filling the bladder increases injury risk. D is wrong - the client wears a gown, not no clothing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for a CT scan with IV contrast and reports a prior severe reaction to contrast dye. The PN should:
options: Proceed with the scan since reactions rarely recur
Report the history to the RN immediately; premedication or alternative imaging may be needed
Reassure the client that contrast reactions are harmless
Give Benadryl without an order before the scan
explain: Correct: B - prior contrast reactions predict future ones; the team must decide on premedication or alternatives. A is wrong - reactions commonly recur and can be worse. C is wrong - severe reactions can be life-threatening. D is wrong - premedication requires orders.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After an upper endoscopy (EGD) with sedation, the PN should check which finding before offering fluids?
options: Blood pressure only
Return of the gag reflex
Bowel sounds
Urine output
explain: Correct: B - the gag reflex must return before oral intake to prevent aspiration after throat anesthesia. A alone is insufficient. C is unrelated to EGD recovery. D does not determine swallow safety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which items must be verified before a client goes for an invasive procedure? Select all that apply.
options: Signed informed consent on the chart
NPO status as ordered
Known allergies documented and communicated
Correct site marking when applicable
The client's favorite music playing
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - consent, NPO, allergies, and site marking are Universal Protocol safety checks. E is wrong - music preference is comfort, not a safety verification.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a lumbar puncture, which PN actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the client flat as ordered
Encouraging fluids as permitted
Monitoring the puncture site for drainage or bleeding
Reporting severe headache, numbness, or weakness to the RN
Encouraging the client to sit upright immediately
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - flat positioning, hydration, site monitoring, and reporting neuro symptoms are correct post-LP care. E is wrong - sitting upright immediately can worsen post-dural puncture headache.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest IV infiltration that the PN should report? Select all that apply.
options: Swelling around the IV site
Coolness and pallor of the surrounding skin
Pain or tenderness at the site
Blood return in the tubing with free flow
Taut, shiny skin over the area
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - swelling, cool pale skin, pain, and taut shiny skin indicate fluid entering tissue. D is wrong - blood return with free flow suggests a patent line, not infiltration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a procedure requiring NPO, the PN learns the client drank juice 2 hours ago. What should the PN do?
options: Say nothing; a little juice will not matter
Report it to the RN immediately; the procedure may need to be delayed due to aspiration risk
Give the client more juice to settle the stomach
Document that the client was NPO
explain: Correct: B - recent intake before anesthesia/sedation risks aspiration; the team must know. A is wrong - any intake matters. C is wrong - more intake worsens the problem. D is wrong - false documentation is fraud.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client reports new calf pain and the PN notes unilateral swelling. What should the PN do?
options: Massage the calf to relieve the pain
Keep the client on bed rest, avoid massaging the leg, and report to the RN promptly as possible DVT
Encourage vigorous leg exercises
Apply heat and reassess tomorrow
explain: Correct: B - unilateral calf pain with swelling suggests DVT; massage could dislodge a clot, so the leg is left alone and the RN notified. A is wrong - massage risks embolization. C is wrong - vigorous exercise is unsafe with suspected DVT. D is wrong - waiting delays diagnosis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is assisting the RN with a blood transfusion check. The PN's role includes:
options: Skipping the identity check to save time
Verifying client identity with two identifiers and matching the blood product label with the RN per policy
Hanging the blood without any verification
Deciding the transfusion rate independently
explain: Correct: B - two-nurse verification of identity and product is the critical safety step. A is wrong - skipping checks risks fatal mismatch. C is wrong - unverified transfusion is never acceptable. D is wrong - the rate follows orders and protocol.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client reports leg pain that starts with walking and stops with rest. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Venous insufficiency
Intermittent claudication from peripheral arterial disease, which should be reported to the RN
A muscle strain needing no report
Arthritis that requires no follow-up
explain: Correct: B - reproducible exertional pain relieved by rest is classic arterial claudication and needs evaluation. A is wrong - venous disease causes aching with prolonged standing, relieved by elevation. C and D dismiss a vascular symptom that warrants workup.

q: The PN is caring for a client with Parkinson's disease. Which observation requires extra safety planning and RN notification?
options: Mild hand tremor at rest
Shuffling gait with freezing episodes and recent near-falls
Soft speech
Taking medication on schedule
explain: Correct: B - freezing gait with near-falls is a major injury risk needing plan adjustment. A and C are expected Parkinson's features to document and accommodate. D is good adherence, not a problem.

q: A client with hypothyroidism reports increasing fatigue, cold intolerance, and constipation. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client these are unrelated to thyroid disease
Document the symptoms and report them to the RN; they may indicate inadequate hormone replacement
Advise the client to stop thyroid medication
Suggest the client just needs more sleep
explain: Correct: B - these are classic hypothyroid symptoms suggesting the replacement dose needs provider review. A is wrong - they are directly related. C is wrong - stopping hormone is dangerous. D is wrong - dismissing symptoms misses the clinical picture.

q: A client with hyperthyroidism develops a temperature of 104 F, severe tachycardia, and extreme agitation. The PN should:
options: Document and recheck in an hour
Recognize possible thyroid storm and notify the RN immediately
Give a warm blanket for comfort
Encourage the client to ambulate
explain: Correct: B - thyroid storm is a life-threatening emergency needing immediate intervention. A is wrong - waiting with these vitals is unsafe. C is wrong - warming worsens hyperthermia. D is wrong - exertion stresses an already overdriven heart.

q: A client with Cushing syndrome is at increased risk for which complications the PN should monitor for?
options: Hypoglycemia and weight loss
Hyperglycemia, hypertension, fragile skin, and infection
Hypothermia and bradycardia
Dehydration with low blood sugar
explain: Correct: B - cortisol excess causes hyperglycemia, hypertension, thin fragile skin, and immunosuppression. A describes the opposite pattern. C suggests hypothyroidism. D is not characteristic of Cushing's.

q: A client with a peptic ulcer reports black tarry stools and feeling faint. The PN should:
options: Offer an antacid and continue routine care
Report immediately; melena with lightheadedness suggests active GI bleeding
Suggest the client eat a large meal
Document it for the next shift
explain: Correct: B - melena plus presyncope signals significant blood loss needing urgent evaluation. A is wrong - an antacid does not address bleeding. C is wrong - eating does not treat hemorrhage. D is wrong - waiting a shift is unsafe.

q: A client reports severe right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal, radiating to the right shoulder, with nausea. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Appendicitis
Cholecystitis, which should be reported to the RN
A kidney stone
Gastritis that needs no report
explain: Correct: B - post-fatty-meal RUQ pain with shoulder radiation is classic gallbladder disease. A is RLQ pain. C is flank pain radiating to the groin. D is wrong - this presentation warrants evaluation, not dismissal.

q: A client with a kidney stone reports severe flank pain radiating to the groin. The PN should:
options: Restrict fluids to reduce urine output
Encourage fluids as ordered, strain all urine, manage pain per orders, and report fever or inability to void
Tell the client the stone will pass without any monitoring
Apply heat to the abdomen and send the client home
explain: Correct: B - hydration, straining to catch the stone, ordered pain control, and reporting obstruction/infection signs are correct. A is wrong - fluid restriction worsens stone passage. C is wrong - monitoring for complications is essential. D is wrong - the PN does not discharge clients.

q: A client with a leg cast reports pain that is severe and out of proportion to the injury, with pale cool toes. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client that cast pain is normal
Report immediately; these suggest compartment syndrome, a surgical emergency
Give extra padding inside the cast
Elevate the leg and recheck tomorrow
explain: Correct: B - pain out of proportion with pallor and coolness signals compartment syndrome needing urgent fasciotomy evaluation. A is wrong - this pain pattern is never 'normal.' C is wrong - adding padding does not relieve compartment pressure. D is wrong - waiting risks tissue death.

q: After hip replacement surgery, the PN reinforces which precautions?
options: Cross the legs to stay comfortable
Keep the operative leg abducted with a pillow between the knees, avoid bending the hip past 90 degrees, and do not cross the legs
Sit in a low soft chair
Twist the body while the feet stay planted
explain: Correct: B - abduction, no hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, and no leg crossing prevent dislocation. A is wrong - crossing risks dislocation. C is wrong - low chairs force excessive hip flexion. D is wrong - twisting stresses the new joint.

q: A client receiving chemotherapy has an absolute neutrophil count of 400/mm3 and a temperature of 101.5 F. The PN should:
options: Document the fever and recheck tomorrow
Report the fever immediately; neutropenic fever is an emergency
Give aspirin without an order
Encourage the client to visit with many friends
explain: Correct: B - fever with severe neutropenia signals possible sepsis and needs immediate evaluation and cultures. A is wrong - waiting is dangerous. C is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope, and aspirin is avoided with bleeding risk. D is wrong - crowds expose the client to infection.

q: An older adult with type 2 diabetes is extremely thirsty, confused, and dehydrated with a glucose of 950 mg/dL and no fruity breath. The PN should recognize this as most consistent with:
options: Hypoglycemia
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS), requiring immediate RN notification
Diabetic ketoacidosis with ketosis
Normal aging
explain: Correct: B - profound hyperglycemia with severe dehydration and altered mental status without ketosis is HHS, an emergency. A is wrong - glucose is critically high, not low. C is wrong - DKA features ketosis with fruity breath, less typical here. D is wrong - this is a metabolic emergency, not aging.

q: A client with SIADH has a sodium of 122 mEq/L and is confused. The PN should:
options: Encourage large amounts of water
Follow fluid restriction orders, monitor I&O and neuro status, and report worsening confusion to the RN
Give salty snacks freely without direction
Ignore the confusion as expected
explain: Correct: B - SIADH causes water retention and dilutional hyponatremia; fluids are restricted and neuro status watched closely. A is wrong - extra water worsens hyponatremia. C is wrong - sodium management follows orders, not free snacking. D is wrong - confusion with Na 122 needs close monitoring.

q: Two days after a femur fracture, a client develops sudden dyspnea, confusion, and petechiae on the chest. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client and continue routine care
Report immediately; this triad suggests fat embolism syndrome, an emergency
Encourage deep breathing and recheck tomorrow
Apply oxygen without an order and say nothing
explain: Correct: B - dyspnea, neuro changes, and petechiae after long-bone fracture are classic fat embolism needing urgent care. A is wrong - this is not routine. C is wrong - waiting risks death. D is wrong - the PN reports emergencies rather than acting silently; oxygen per protocol with notification.

q: Which findings suggest arterial insufficiency in the legs? Select all that apply.
options: Cool, pale extremities with diminished pulses
Pain with walking relieved by rest
Shiny skin with hair loss on the legs
Brownish skin discoloration around the ankles
Aching that worsens with prolonged standing and improves with elevation
explain: Correct: A, B, C - cool pallor, weak pulses, claudication, and trophic skin changes indicate arterial disease. D is wrong - brown ankle discoloration suggests venous stasis. E is wrong - aching relieved by elevation is venous, not arterial.

q: Which findings are consistent with hyperthyroidism? Select all that apply.
options: Unexplained weight loss
Heat intolerance and diaphoresis
Tachycardia and nervousness
Exophthalmos (bulging eyes)
Cold intolerance and lethargy
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - weight loss, heat intolerance, tachycardia, anxiety, and eye changes reflect thyroid hormone excess. E is wrong - cold intolerance and lethargy indicate hypothyroidism, the opposite.

q: Which ulcer complications must the PN report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Black tarry stools
Coffee-ground emesis
Sudden severe abdominal pain with a rigid abdomen
Hypotension and tachycardia
Mild heartburn after a spicy meal
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - melena, coffee-ground emesis, rigid abdomen (perforation), and shock vitals are emergencies. E is wrong - mild heartburn alone is not a complication.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client passing a kidney stone. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will drink plenty of fluids as instructed
I will strain all my urine to catch the stone
I will report fever, chills, or inability to urinate
I should restrict all fluids to rest my kidneys
Severe unrelieved pain is expected and needs no report
explain: Correct: A, B, C - hydration, straining, and reporting obstruction/infection signs are correct. D is wrong - fluid restriction hinders stone passage. E is wrong - uncontrolled pain needs reassessment and reporting.

q: Which findings suggest compartment syndrome that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Pain out of proportion to the injury
Pallor and coolness of the extremity
Paresthesia or numbness
Weak or absent distal pulse
Mild swelling that improves with elevation
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - the '6 Ps' pattern (pain, pallor, paresthesia, pulselessness, plus paralysis/poikilothermia) signals compartment syndrome. E is wrong - mild swelling that improves with elevation is expected post-injury, not compartment syndrome.

q: Which precautions are appropriate for a neutropenic client? Select all that apply.
options: Strict hand hygiene by everyone entering the room
Avoiding crowds and visitors who are ill
Reporting any fever immediately
Avoiding fresh flowers and raw fruits/vegetables per policy
Sharing eating utensils to build immunity
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - hand hygiene, avoiding exposures, fever surveillance, and avoiding environmental sources of pathogens protect neutropenic clients. E is wrong - sharing utensils spreads infection; it does not build immunity.

q: Which findings suggest Addisonian crisis that the PN must report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Severe hypotension unresponsive to fluids per protocol
Profound weakness and confusion
Dehydration with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia
Fever
Hypertension and fluid retention
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - refractory hypotension, neuro changes, electrolyte derangement, and fever mark adrenal crisis. E is wrong - hypertension with fluid retention suggests cortisol excess (Cushing's), the opposite of adrenal failure.

q: The PN reinforces hip replacement precautions. Which client statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will keep a pillow between my knees
I will not cross my legs
I will avoid bending my hip past 90 degrees
I will sit in low, soft chairs
I will report sudden severe hip pain or a popping sensation
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - abduction pillow, no leg crossing, limited hip flexion, and reporting dislocation signs are correct. D is wrong - low soft chairs force hip flexion beyond 90 degrees and risk dislocation.

q: The PN walks into a room and finds a client unresponsive and not breathing. What is the PN's first action?
options: Run to find the RN
Call for help, begin CPR per BLS training, and ensure the code team is activated
Wait for the provider to arrive
Document the finding first
explain: Correct: B - the PN initiates BLS immediately while help is summoned; seconds matter. A is wrong - leaving to find the RN delays resuscitation. C is wrong - waiting for the provider wastes critical time. D is wrong - documentation never precedes lifesaving action.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The rapid response team criteria include a client with sudden chest pain and dropping oxygen saturation. The PN should:
options: Wait for the next scheduled vital sign check
Stay with the client, call the rapid response team per policy, and notify the RN
Tell the client to calm down and breathe slowly
Give a sedative to reduce anxiety
explain: Correct: B - rapid response exists for exactly this deterioration; the PN activates it and stays. A is wrong - waiting through a crisis is unsafe. C is wrong - reassurance alone does not address the emergency. D is wrong - sedating without orders and assessment is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A provider's handwritten order is illegible. The PN should:
options: Guess the meaning based on context
Ask another PN what they think it says
Contact the provider for clarification before acting
Skip the order entirely
explain: Correct: C - illegible orders must be clarified with the prescriber; never guess. A and B are wrong - guessing or crowdsourcing an order risks serious error. D is wrong - ignoring a possibly needed order without clarification is also unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN receives a verbal order in an emergency. The correct practice is to:
options: Act immediately without repeating it
Repeat the order back to the prescriber for confirmation and document it per policy
Have the UAP carry it out
Write it down later from memory
explain: Correct: B - read-back verification prevents misheard orders, and timely documentation is required. A is wrong - acting without confirmation risks error. C is wrong - UAPs do not carry out orders. D is wrong - delayed memory-based charting is inaccurate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A competent client with no advance directive suddenly loses consciousness. The team begins resuscitation. The PN's role is to:
options: Stop the resuscitation until the family arrives
Participate in the assigned code role and document objectively afterward
Decide the client would not want resuscitation
Leave the room to avoid involvement
explain: Correct: B - without a valid DNR, full resuscitation proceeds; the PN fulfills the assigned role and documents. A is wrong - waiting for family delays lifesaving care. C is wrong - the PN cannot presume the client's wishes. D is wrong - abandoning the code team is unacceptable.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is floated to a pediatric unit. The PN has only adult experience. What is the best action?
options: Accept any assignment; nursing is nursing
Inform the charge nurse of the experience gap and accept only assignments matching PN competence, such as stable clients
Refuse to enter the unit
Perform unfamiliar pediatric procedures to learn quickly
explain: Correct: B - the PN practices within competence and communicates limits so assignments are safe. A is wrong - adult and pediatric care differ significantly. C is wrong - outright refusal is unnecessary when safe assignments exist. D is wrong - learning unfamiliar procedures on children is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client reports that another staff member was rude and rough during care. The PN should:
options: Promise the client the staff member will be fired
Listen, document the client's report objectively, and notify the RN/charge nurse per policy
Tell the client they are imagining it
Confront the staff member aggressively
explain: Correct: B - the PN takes the report seriously, documents objectively, and escalates through proper channels. A is wrong - the PN cannot promise employment outcomes. C is wrong - dismissing the report invalidates the client. D is wrong - aggressive confrontation is unprofessional.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notices a colleague documenting care that was not provided. This is:
options: Acceptable if the colleague is busy
Falsification of the medical record, which the PN must report through the chain of command
A private matter between colleagues
Only a problem if the client is harmed
explain: Correct: B - false documentation is fraud and endangers clients; it must be reported. A is wrong - busyness never justifies falsification. C is wrong - it is a patient-safety and legal issue, not private. D is wrong - the act itself is the violation, regardless of outcome.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When a client is transferred to another unit, the PN's responsibilities include:
options: Sending the client alone with belongings
Providing a handoff report, ensuring records and belongings accompany the client, and confirming receipt
Keeping the transfer secret from the family
Documenting only after the next shift
explain: Correct: B - safe transfer needs handoff communication, complete records, belongings, and confirmed receipt. A is wrong - clients are never sent alone without report. C is wrong - families are informed per client wishes and policy. D is wrong - documentation must be timely.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family asks the PN to recommend a nursing home for discharge. The PN should:
options: Recommend the facility the PN's relative works at
Refer the request to the RN/discharge planner who coordinates placement resources
Refuse to help at all
Choose the cheapest facility
explain: Correct: B - discharge placement is coordinated by the RN/discharge planner with appropriate resources. A is wrong - personal referrals are a conflict of interest. C is wrong - refusing help abandons the family. D is wrong - cost alone does not determine suitability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to participate in a research study recruitment on the unit. The PN's appropriate role is to:
options: Enroll clients without telling them it is research
Provide only IRB-approved information and refer interested clients to the research team; never coerce
Promise clients the study will cure them
Enroll only clients who cannot refuse
explain: Correct: B - the PN shares approved information and refers; consent belongs to the research team and participation is voluntary. A is wrong - hidden enrollment violates informed consent. C is wrong - promising cures is coercive and false. D is wrong - targeting vulnerable clients is unethical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with dementia is being discharged to a family caregiver. The PN's best contribution is to:
options: Provide the initial comprehensive discharge teaching
Reinforce the teaching the RN provided, using simple steps and teach-back, and report caregiver concerns to the RN
Tell the family they are on their own
Write new discharge instructions independently
explain: Correct: B - the PN reinforces with teach-back and reports concerns; initial teaching is the RN's role. A is wrong - initial discharge teaching belongs to the RN. C is wrong - abandoning the caregiver is unacceptable. D is wrong - the PN does not create independent discharge plans.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN overhears a provider making a derogatory comment about a client. The PN should:
options: Laugh along to fit in
Not participate, continue professional care, and report the behavior per facility policy
Repeat the comment to the client
Post about it on social media
explain: Correct: B - the PN upholds professionalism, keeps care unbiased, and reports through proper channels. A is wrong - joining in is unprofessional. C is wrong - repeating it harms the client. D is wrong - social media posts violate confidentiality and policy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which assignments are appropriate for the PN? Select all that apply.
options: A stable client needing routine wound care and vital signs
Reinforcing teaching for a client with a new diagnosis, after the RN's initial teaching
Collecting data on a client with stable chronic illness
Independently managing a client on multiple titratable IV drips
Performing the initial assessment of an unstable emergency department client
explain: Correct: A, B, C - stable clients needing routine care, data collection, and teaching reinforcement fit PN scope. D is wrong - titratable drips need RN management. E is wrong - unstable initial assessments belong to the RN.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN suspects a colleague is impaired at work. What should the PN do? Select all that apply.
options: Report the concern to the supervisor per policy
Document objective observations factually
Confront the colleague publicly on the unit
Continue to let the colleague care for clients alone
Follow the facility's impaired-practitioner reporting process
explain: Correct: A, B, E - reporting to the supervisor, factual documentation, and following the impaired-practitioner process protect clients. C is wrong - public confrontation is unprofessional and unsafe. D is wrong - an impaired colleague must not practice unsupervised.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions demonstrate the PN's role in quality improvement? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting near misses and adverse events
Following evidence-based protocols consistently
Suggesting workflow improvements to the manager
Hiding errors to protect the unit's reputation
Participating in unit-based safety huddles
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - event reporting, protocol adherence, improvement suggestions, and safety huddles all advance quality. D is wrong - hiding errors prevents learning and endangers clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is being discharged with new prescriptions. The PN's appropriate actions include: Select all that apply.
options: Reinforcing the medication schedule the RN and pharmacist taught
Using teach-back to confirm understanding
Writing new prescriptions for the client
Reporting confusion or barriers to the RN
Telling the client to skip doses that cause mild side effects
explain: Correct: A, B, D - reinforcing the taught schedule, teach-back verification, and reporting barriers are PN roles. C is wrong - the PN does not prescribe. E is wrong - the PN never advises skipping doses; side effects are reported to the RN/provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements about delegation are true? Select all that apply.
options: The nurse retains accountability for delegated tasks
Only stable clients with predictable outcomes are appropriate for delegation to UAPs
Assessment, evaluation, and teaching cannot be delegated to UAPs
The nurse must verify the UAP's competence for the task
Delegation means the nurse no longer needs to follow up
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - accountability stays with the nurse, delegation fits stable predictable situations, clinical judgment tasks stay with licensed staff, and competence must be verified. E is wrong - follow-up and supervision are required; delegation never ends oversight.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When removing PPE, the correct order is:
options: Mask first, then gown, then gloves
Gloves first, then gown, then eye protection, then mask, with hand hygiene
Gown first, then mask, then gloves
All items at once in any order
explain: Correct: B - most contaminated items come off first (gloves, then gown), then eye protection and mask, with hand hygiene during and after. A is wrong - the mask is removed last to protect the airway longest. C and D ignore contamination principles.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is receiving sealed internal radiation therapy. The PN should apply which principle?
options: Spend as much time as possible in the room for support
Limit time near the client, maximize distance, and use shielding per policy
Allow children to visit freely
Remove the radiation source if the client is uncomfortable
explain: Correct: B - time, distance, and shielding minimize exposure. A is wrong - prolonged close contact increases exposure. C is wrong - children and pregnant visitors are restricted. D is wrong - only specially trained staff handle sources.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN hears a bed alarm but is busy with another client. What should the PN do?
options: Ignore it; someone else will respond
Ask available staff to check immediately or go as soon as safely possible; alarms are never ignored
Turn off all alarms to reduce noise
Assume it is a false alarm
explain: Correct: B - every alarm needs a response; the PN delegates the check or responds directly. A is wrong - assuming others will respond is how falls happen. C is wrong - disabling alarms is dangerous. D is wrong - alarms are treated as real until assessed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A visitor becomes verbally threatening toward staff. The PN's best action is to:
options: Argue with the visitor to defend the staff
Stay calm, do not engage physically, seek help per the facility's workplace violence policy
Lock the visitor in a room
Ignore the threats completely
explain: Correct: B - de-escalation, disengagement, and following the violence policy protect everyone. A is wrong - arguing escalates danger. C is wrong - confining a visitor is inappropriate and unsafe. D is wrong - threats must be reported, not ignored.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about storing medications at home. The key points include:
options: Store medications in a locked, high cabinet away from children, in original labeled containers
Transfer pills into unlabeled decorative containers for convenience
Share prescriptions with family to save money
Store all pills in the bathroom medicine cabinet regardless of heat and humidity
explain: Correct: A - locked, elevated storage in original labeled containers prevents pediatric poisoning and mix-ups. B is wrong - unlabeled containers cause dangerous confusion. C is wrong - sharing prescriptions is dangerous. D is wrong - heat and humidity degrade many drugs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: An infant abduction prevention measure the PN should follow is:
options: Letting anyone carry the infant to the nursery
Verifying identification bands match before handing the infant to anyone and following unit security procedures
Removing the infant's ID band for comfort
Allowing visitors to take the infant off the unit freely
explain: Correct: B - band verification and security procedures prevent abduction. A is wrong - only authorized staff transport infants. C is wrong - ID bands stay on. D is wrong - infants never leave the unit with visitors unchecked.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN smells gas in the hallway. What is the first action?
options: Light a match to find the leak
Evacuate the area, avoid sparks and electrical switches, and report per emergency procedures
Open all windows and continue working
Use the elevator to leave quickly
explain: Correct: B - gas leaks need evacuation without ignition sources and proper reporting. A is wrong - open flame near gas is catastrophic. C is wrong - staying in the area is unsafe. D is wrong - elevators can spark; stairs are used.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has norovirus. Which precautions should the PN follow?
options: Airborne precautions with N95
Contact precautions with gown and gloves, plus careful hand hygiene with soap and water
No precautions are needed after symptoms stop for one hour
Droplet precautions only
explain: Correct: B - norovirus spreads by contact; gown, gloves, and soap-and-water hand hygiene are required. A is wrong - it is not airborne. C is wrong - shedding continues after symptoms resolve and precautions follow policy duration. D is wrong - droplet alone is insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN needs to move a heavy, immobile client up in bed. The safest approach is to:
options: Pull the client up alone by the arms
Use a friction-reducing draw sheet with enough staff, keeping the back straight
Drag the client by the legs
Ask the client to pull on the IV pole
explain: Correct: B - draw sheets with adequate staff and good body mechanics prevent injury to client and nurse. A is wrong - pulling arms injures shoulders. C is wrong - dragging causes skin tears. D is wrong - IV poles are not lift devices and the line could dislodge.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which factors increase a client's fall risk that the PN should assess and report? Select all that apply.
options: History of previous falls
Orthostatic hypotension
Impaired vision or hearing
Use of sedating medications
Wearing well-fitting nonskid footwear
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - fall history, orthostatic drops, sensory impairment, and sedating drugs all raise fall risk. E is wrong - proper nonskid footwear reduces risk; it is protective, not a risk factor.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which practices prevent needlestick injuries? Select all that apply.
options: Never recapping used needles
Disposing of sharps immediately in puncture-resistant containers
Using safety-engineered devices as available
Carrying used needles to a distant disposal container by hand
Keeping sharps containers within arm's reach during procedures
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - no recapping, immediate disposal, safety devices, and nearby containers prevent sticks. D is wrong - carrying exposed sharps across distances invites injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which infant home safety points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Crib slats no more than 2-3/8 inches apart
No soft bedding, pillows, or stuffed animals in the crib
Water heater set no higher than 120 F
Leaving the infant unattended in the bathtub briefly
Keeping small objects and cords out of reach
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - safe crib spacing, bare crib, safe water temperature, and choking/strangulation prevention are key. D is wrong - infants must never be left unattended in water, even briefly.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 7-month-old cries when a stranger tries to hold them. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Abnormal attachment
Normal stranger anxiety, a healthy developmental milestone
A sign of illness
Evidence of poor parenting
explain: Correct: B - stranger anxiety peaks around 6-9 months and signals healthy attachment. A is wrong - it is not abnormal. C is wrong - it is developmental, not illness. D is wrong - it does not reflect parenting quality.

q: A toddler plays alongside other children but not with them. This is called:
options: Cooperative play
Parallel play, which is normal for toddlers
Solitary play indicating a problem
Aggressive play
explain: Correct: B - parallel play is the expected toddler pattern. A is wrong - cooperative play comes later, in school age. C is wrong - parallel play is normal, not problematic. D mislabels the behavior.

q: The major psychosocial task of the preschool years, per Erikson, is:
options: Trust vs. mistrust
Initiative vs. guilt
Industry vs. inferiority
Intimacy vs. isolation
explain: Correct: B - preschoolers develop initiative through imaginative play and exploration. A is infancy. C is school age. D is young adulthood.

q: A school-age child is proud of completing a science project. Per Erikson, the child is developing:
options: Autonomy
Industry vs. inferiority
Identity
Generativity
explain: Correct: B - school-age children build industry through competence and accomplishment. A is toddlerhood. C is adolescence. D is middle adulthood.

q: An adolescent spends most time with a peer group and adopts their styles. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Dangerous rebellion
Normal identity development through peer affiliation
A sign of family failure
Evidence of low intelligence
explain: Correct: B - peer groups are central to adolescent identity formation. A is wrong - it is not inherently dangerous. C is wrong - it does not indicate family failure. D is irrelevant and judgmental.

q: Per Erikson, the older adult reflecting on life with satisfaction is achieving:
options: Despair
Integrity vs. despair
Stagnation
Role confusion
explain: Correct: B - integrity is the positive resolution of the older adult stage. A is the negative outcome. C is middle adulthood's negative pole. D is adolescence.

q: The PN reinforces cervical cancer screening teaching. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: Screening starts at age 21 regardless of sexual history, per current guidelines
Screening is only needed after menopause
One normal Pap test means no further screening ever
Screening is unnecessary with the HPV vaccine
explain: Correct: A - guidelines recommend starting Pap screening at 21. B is wrong - screening spans ages 21-65. C is wrong - screening continues at intervals after normal results. D is wrong - vaccination does not eliminate screening need.

q: The PN reinforces prostate screening teaching for a 55-year-old male. The correct approach is:
options: Screening decisions should be individualized through shared decision-making with the provider
No man ever needs prostate screening
Screening is mandatory at 40 for everyone
Only men with symptoms need discussion
explain: Correct: A - guidelines favor informed shared decision-making about PSA screening. B is wrong - screening has a role for many men. C is wrong - there is no universal mandatory age. D is wrong - waiting for symptoms misses early detection.

q: A hospitalized 5-year-old starts wetting the bed after being toilet trained. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Regression, a defense mechanism under stress
Deliberate misbehavior
A neurological emergency
A sign the child was never trained
explain: Correct: A - regression to earlier behaviors under stress is common and usually temporary. B is wrong - it is not willful mischief. C is wrong - stress-related regression is not a neuro emergency. D is wrong - prior training was achieved; stress caused the lapse.

q: A client yells at the PN after receiving bad news from the provider. The PN recognizes this as possibly:
options: Psychosis
Displacement of anger onto a safer target
A personality disorder
Normal communication
explain: Correct: B - displacement redirects emotion from its true source to a safer one. A is wrong - anger alone is not psychosis. C is wrong - one outburst does not diagnose a disorder. D is wrong - yelling at the nurse is not effective communication.

q: A client channels anger about illness into raising money for disease research. This is an example of:
options: Denial
Sublimation, a mature defense mechanism
Projection
Repression
explain: Correct: B - sublimation converts unacceptable impulses into productive activity. A is wrong - the client acknowledges the illness. C is wrong - nothing is attributed to others. D is wrong - the feelings are consciously redirected, not buried.

q: A client with autism is admitted. Which PN approaches are best?
options: Change the routine frequently to build flexibility
Maintain predictable routines, use simple clear language, and minimize sensory overload
Avoid all communication to reduce stress
Insist on eye contact during teaching
explain: Correct: B - predictability, simple language, and sensory management support clients with autism. A is wrong - frequent changes increase distress. C is wrong - communication should be adapted, not avoided. D is wrong - forced eye contact causes discomfort.

q: An anxious client is overwhelmed by too many choices. The PN's best approach is to:
options: Make all decisions for the client
Offer limited, simple choices to reduce overwhelm while preserving autonomy
Present ten options to distract the client
Tell the client anxiety is a choice
explain: Correct: B - limited choices lower anxiety while respecting autonomy. A is wrong - total decision-making removes autonomy. C is wrong - more options worsen overwhelm. D is wrong - anxiety is not a voluntary choice.

q: A client with a phobia of needles needs blood drawn. The PN's best initial action is to:
options: Hold the client down for the draw
Acknowledge the fear, explain each step, use a calm approach, and notify the RN of the phobia
Cancel all blood work permanently
Tell the client the fear is irrational
explain: Correct: B - validation, information, and calm technique reduce fear; the RN coordinates the plan. A is wrong - force traumatizes and can be battery. C is wrong - needed labs cannot be permanently canceled by the PN. D is wrong - calling fear irrational is nontherapeutic.

q: Which findings suggest a client's depression is improving? Select all that apply.
options: Renewed interest in hobbies and socializing
Improved appetite and sleep
Talking about future plans
Sudden calm after a period of deep despair
Giving away prized possessions
explain: Correct: A, B, C - returning interest, better sleep/appetite, and future orientation signal genuine improvement. D is wrong - sudden calm after deep depression may mean a suicide plan was decided, not recovery. E is wrong - giving away possessions is a warning sign.

q: Which communication strategies help when caring for a client with delusions? Select all that apply.
options: Focusing on the feelings behind the delusion rather than arguing its content
Presenting reality calmly without reinforcing the false belief
Encouraging the client to describe the experience
Agreeing the delusion is real to build rapport
Arguing forcefully until the client admits being wrong
explain: Correct: A, B, C - addressing feelings, calm reality presentation, and listening are therapeutic. D is wrong - agreeing reinforces psychosis. E is wrong - arguing increases agitation without changing the belief.

q: The PN is applying anti-embolism stockings. The correct technique is:
options: Apply them wrinkled to improve grip
Apply smoothly without wrinkles, as ordered, and remove periodically to check skin
Leave them on for a week without removal
Apply only at night
explain: Correct: B - smooth application prevents pressure injury; periodic removal allows skin checks. A is wrong - wrinkles cause skin breakdown. C is wrong - prolonged wear without checks is unsafe. D is wrong - they are typically worn during the day or per orders.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is turning an immobile client. The correct schedule and technique include:
options: Turning every 2 hours using proper body mechanics and support devices
Turning once per shift
Dragging the client across the sheets
Leaving the client in one position all night for rest
explain: Correct: A - q2h turning with good mechanics prevents pressure injuries and staff harm. B is wrong - once per shift is far too infrequent. C is wrong - dragging causes shear and skin tears. D is wrong - prolonged positioning causes breakdown.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN gives a back rub to a client on bed rest. The primary purposes are:
options: Diagnosing skin cancer
Promoting comfort, circulation, and relaxation while allowing skin assessment
Replacing the need for repositioning
Curing muscle disease
explain: Correct: B - back rubs comfort, stimulate circulation, relax, and offer skin inspection time. A is wrong - back rubs do not diagnose cancer. C is wrong - they supplement, not replace, turning. D is wrong - they do not cure disease.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client's eyeglasses. The correct practice is to:
options: Clean them with a soft cloth, store them in a labeled case when not worn, and ensure the client can reach them
Clean them with paper towels and ammonia
Store them loose in the bed linens
Keep them at the nurses' station
explain: Correct: A - soft cloth cleaning, protective labeled case, and accessibility prevent damage and loss. B is wrong - harsh chemicals scratch lenses. C is wrong - linens hide and crush glasses. D is wrong - the client needs them accessible, not locked away.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing bladder training for a client with incontinence. The correct approach is:
options: Catheterize the client permanently
Use a timed voiding schedule, gradually lengthening intervals, and report progress to the RN
Restrict all fluids
Tell the client incontinence is untreatable
explain: Correct: B - scheduled toileting with gradually extended intervals retrains the bladder. A is wrong - permanent catheterization is a last resort with infection risk. C is wrong - fluid restriction worsens incontinence and dehydration. D is wrong - bladder training is effective for many clients.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has bilateral leg edema. The PN should position the client to:
options: Keep the legs dependent at all times
Elevate the legs above heart level periodically to promote venous return
Cross the legs for comfort
Keep the client standing most of the day
explain: Correct: B - elevation above heart level aids venous return and reduces edema. A is wrong - dependency worsens edema. C is wrong - crossing impedes venous flow. D is wrong - prolonged standing increases edema.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a client onto a bedpan. The most comfortable and effective position is:
options: Flat in bed
Head of bed elevated as tolerated to use gravity and abdominal muscles
Trendelenburg
Standing beside the bed
explain: Correct: B - elevating the head uses gravity and allows abdominal muscle use for elimination. A is wrong - flat positioning makes elimination difficult. C is wrong - Trendelenburg is for shock, not toileting. D is nonsensical for bedpan use.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures promote rest and sleep for hospitalized clients? Select all that apply.
options: Clustering care to allow uninterrupted rest periods
Reducing noise and dimming lights at night
Offering a back rub or warm drink as appropriate
Scheduling all procedures in the middle of the night
Keeping the television loud all night
explain: Correct: A, B, C - clustered care, quiet dark environment, and comfort measures promote sleep. D is wrong - nighttime procedures fragment sleep unnecessarily. E is wrong - loud TV disrupts sleep.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions help prevent skin tears in older adults? Select all that apply.
options: Handling limbs gently without pulling
Keeping skin moisturized
Avoiding adhesive tape directly on fragile skin
Wearing long sleeves during transfers
Scrubbing the skin vigorously during bathing
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - gentle handling, moisturized skin, tape alternatives, and protective clothing prevent tears. E is wrong - vigorous scrubbing injures fragile skin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a weak client with ambulation. Which practices are safe? Select all that apply.
options: Using a gait belt
Walking slightly behind and to the side of the client
Ensuring the client wears nonskid footwear
Rushing the client to finish quickly
Checking that the path is clear of obstacles
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - gait belt, proper guarding position, safe footwear, and clear paths prevent falls. D is wrong - rushing a weak client causes falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client uses a corticosteroid inhaler daily. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Stop the inhaler once breathing feels better
Rinse the mouth after each use to prevent oral thrush
Use it only during severe attacks
Share the inhaler with family members
explain: Correct: B - rinsing prevents candida infection from deposited steroid. A is wrong - controller inhalers are daily maintenance, not stopped when better. C is wrong - rescue inhalers are for attacks; steroids are controllers. D is wrong - inhalers are never shared.

q: A client takes glipizide for type 2 diabetes. The PN reinforces that it should be taken:
options: At bedtime
30 minutes before breakfast, since it stimulates insulin release with the meal
Only when glucose is high
With a large sugary snack
explain: Correct: B - glipizide is taken before meals so insulin release matches food intake. A is wrong - bedtime dosing risks overnight hypoglycemia without food. C is wrong - it is scheduled therapy, not sliding scale. D is wrong - sugary snacks defeat glucose control.

q: A client receives lorazepam for anxiety. The PN's priority safety action is to:
options: Encourage the client to drive to reduce anxiety
Implement fall precautions and monitor for excessive sedation, reporting concerns to the RN
Give extra doses if the client still feels anxious
Tell the client sedation is impossible with this drug
explain: Correct: B - benzodiazepines sedate and impair balance; fall precautions and sedation monitoring are essential. A is wrong - driving while sedated is dangerous. C is wrong - the PN never gives extra doses. D is wrong - sedation is a primary effect.

q: A client uses timolol eye drops for glaucoma. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Stop the drops once vision feels normal
Use them as prescribed and report eye pain, vision changes, or slow pulse
Share the drops with anyone with eye redness
Use the drops only when the eyes hurt
explain: Correct: B - glaucoma drops are lifelong therapy; eye symptoms and systemic beta-blocker effects (bradycardia) need reporting. A is wrong - stopping risks vision loss. C is wrong - eye medications are never shared. D is wrong - glaucoma is often painless; drops are scheduled.

q: A client takes antacids frequently. The PN reinforces that antacids should be:
options: Taken at the same time as all other medications
Taken 2 hours apart from other medications, since they can impair absorption
Taken in unlimited amounts
Chewed and swallowed without water
explain: Correct: B - antacids bind many drugs; separation preserves absorption. A is wrong - simultaneous dosing reduces other drugs' effectiveness. C is wrong - excess antacids cause electrolyte problems. D is wrong - water aids the antacid's action and esophageal clearance.

q: An IV of 1000 mL is ordered over 8 hours with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What is the drip rate?
options: 15 gtt/min
31 gtt/min
60 gtt/min
125 gtt/min
explain: Correct: B - 1000 mL / 8 hr = 125 mL/hr; (125 x 15) / 60 = 31.25, rounded to 31 gtt/min. A ignores the time factor. C and D reflect calculation errors.

q: A child weighs 15 kg. The order is for 10 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours. How much per dose?
options: 75 mg
150 mg
15 mg
300 mg
explain: Correct: A - 15 kg x 10 mg/kg = 150 mg per day; divided q12h = 75 mg per dose. B is the total daily dose, not per dose. C and D reflect math errors.

q: The PN is reinforcing alendronate teaching for osteoporosis. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will take it in the morning with a full glass of water
I will stay upright for at least 30 minutes afterward
I will take nothing else by mouth until after the 30 minutes
I will take it at bedtime with a snack
I can lie down right after taking it
explain: Correct: A, B, C - full water, upright 30 minutes, and nothing else by mouth prevent esophageal injury. D is wrong - bedtime dosing with food ruins absorption and safety. E is wrong - lying down risks esophageal ulceration.

q: Which findings in a client taking a statin must be reported? Select all that apply.
options: Unexplained muscle pain or tenderness
Dark or tea-colored urine
Severe fatigue with muscle weakness
Mild headache that resolves
Occasional heartburn
explain: Correct: A, B, C - muscle symptoms with dark urine and weakness suggest rhabdomyolysis. D and E are common mild complaints not specific to statin emergencies.

q: Which steps describe correct metered-dose inhaler use? Select all that apply.
options: Shaking the inhaler before use
Exhaling fully before inhaling the dose
Holding the breath about 10 seconds after inhaling
Waiting about a minute between puffs
Inhaling through the nose while pressing the canister
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - shake, exhale, slow deep inhalation with the puff, breath-hold, and spacing puffs optimize delivery. E is wrong - the dose is inhaled through the mouth, not the nose.

q: Which opioid safety points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Storing opioids locked away from others
Never sharing the prescription
Avoiding alcohol while taking opioids
Reporting excessive drowsiness or slow breathing
Driving normally while taking opioids
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - locked storage, no sharing, no alcohol, and reporting respiratory depression are opioid safety essentials. E is wrong - opioids impair alertness; driving is unsafe.

q: A client's sodium is 128 mEq/L with new confusion. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to drink more water
Report to the RN promptly; hyponatremia with neuro changes needs evaluation
Document it as normal
Restrict the client's activity permanently
explain: Correct: B - sodium 128 is below the 135-145 normal range, and confusion signals cerebral effects needing urgent review. A is wrong - extra water worsens dilutional hyponatremia. C is wrong - 128 is abnormal. D is wrong - permanent restriction is not the intervention.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's calcium is 7.2 mg/dL with tingling in the fingers. The PN should:
options: Offer a glass of milk as treatment
Report to the RN promptly; hypocalcemia with symptoms needs evaluation
Tell the client tingling is normal
Encourage vigorous exercise
explain: Correct: B - calcium 7.2 is below the 8.5-10.5 normal range with symptoms; urgent evaluation is needed. A is wrong - milk is not a treatment for symptomatic hypocalcemia. C is wrong - paresthesias are not normal. D is irrelevant and unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before surgery, hair at the operative site needs removal. The PN should ensure:
options: The site is shaved with a razor the night before
Clippers are used per policy, avoiding razors that cause micro-cuts
No hair removal is ever done
The client shaves at home with a dull blade
explain: Correct: B - clippers avoid the micro-abrasions that razors create, reducing infection risk. A is wrong - razor shaving increases surgical site infection. C is wrong - hair is removed when it interferes with surgery. D is wrong - dull home razors are the worst option.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client received sedation for a procedure 2 hours ago and wants to walk to the bathroom alone. The PN should:
options: Allow it; 2 hours is long enough
Assist with ambulation and use fall precautions, since sedation effects linger
Tell the client to hold it until tomorrow
Remove all fall precautions
explain: Correct: B - residual sedation impairs balance; supervised ambulation with precautions is required. A is wrong - time alone does not guarantee recovery. C is wrong - withholding toileting is inappropriate. D is wrong - precautions stay until the client is steady.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's pulse oximetry reads 88% on room air with increased respiratory rate. The PN should:
options: Document it and recheck next shift
Report to the RN immediately and stay with the client; hypoxemia needs urgent evaluation
Remove the probe and assume it is faulty
Tell the client to breathe faster
explain: Correct: B - 88% saturation with tachypnea signals significant hypoxemia requiring immediate action. A is wrong - waiting a shift is unsafe. C is wrong - assuming equipment failure without rechecking wastes time. D is wrong - the client is already tachypneic; coaching faster breathing is not the intervention.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest sepsis that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Fever or hypothermia
Tachycardia
Tachypnea
Hypotension with altered mental status
Normal vital signs with good energy
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - temperature abnormality, tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypotension with mental status changes are sepsis warning signs. E is wrong - normal vitals with good energy do not suggest sepsis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which electrolyte values must the PN report to the RN promptly? Select all that apply.
options: Potassium 2.8 mEq/L
Sodium 128 mEq/L
Calcium 7.0 mg/dL
Magnesium 1.0 mEq/L
Potassium 4.2 mEq/L
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - K 2.8 (low; normal 3.5-5.0), Na 128 (low; normal 135-145), Ca 7.0 (low; normal 8.5-10.5), and Mg 1.0 (low; normal 1.5-2.5) are all abnormal and reportable. E is wrong - K 4.2 is within normal range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which measures help prevent post-op respiratory complications? Select all that apply.
options: Turning, coughing, and deep breathing
Incentive spirometer use as ordered
Early ambulation as ordered
Keeping the client flat and immobile
Encouraging fluids as permitted
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - pulmonary hygiene, spirometry, mobility, and hydration prevent atelectasis and pneumonia. D is wrong - flat immobility promotes respiratory complications.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client's pulse is irregularly irregular. The PN should:
options: Document it as a normal variation
Report it to the RN promptly; new irregular rhythm may indicate atrial fibrillation
Tell the client to exercise to regulate it
Recheck in a week
explain: Correct: B - new irregularly irregular pulse suggests atrial fibrillation, which needs evaluation for rate control and stroke risk. A is wrong - it is not a normal variation. C is wrong - exercise is unsafe with a new dysrhythmia. D is wrong - waiting a week is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client on bed rest suddenly develops sharp chest pain, dyspnea, and tachycardia. The PN should:
options: Encourage deep breathing and recheck later
Keep the client on bed rest, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders; this suggests pulmonary embolism
Massage the legs to improve circulation
Give the client a sedative
explain: Correct: B - sudden pleuritic chest pain with dyspnea and tachycardia in an immobile client suggests PE, an emergency. A is wrong - waiting risks death. C is wrong - leg massage could dislodge more clot. D is wrong - sedation without orders masks symptoms.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has a nasogastric tube with continuous suction. The PN notes the drainage is bright red with clots. The PN should:
options: Document it as normal post-op drainage
Report it to the RN immediately; bright red bloody drainage with clots may indicate active bleeding
Increase the suction pressure
Remove the tube
explain: Correct: B - bright red blood with clots suggests active GI bleeding needing urgent evaluation. A is wrong - this is not normal. C is wrong - changing suction requires orders. D is wrong - the PN does not remove the tube independently.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with atrial fibrillation is at risk for which complication the PN should reinforce teaching about?
options: Hypoglycemia
Stroke from blood clots forming in the atria
Kidney stones
Peptic ulcers
explain: Correct: B - stagnant blood in fibrillating atria forms clots that can embolize to the brain. A, C, and D are unrelated to atrial fibrillation.

q: A client with suspected bacterial meningitis has a severe headache, fever, and stiff neck. The PN should:
options: Place the client in a dark quiet room and delay reporting
Initiate droplet precautions per policy and notify the RN immediately
Give aspirin without an order
Encourage the client to sit upright and read
explain: Correct: B - meningitis is a medical emergency; droplet precautions plus immediate notification are required. A is wrong - delaying care for comfort is unsafe. C is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope. D is irrelevant to the emergency.

q: A client with Guillain-Barre syndrome reports increasing difficulty swallowing and a weak cough. The PN should:
options: Offer a large meal
Report to the RN immediately; ascending weakness can compromise breathing and swallowing
Encourage the client to practice swallowing alone
Document it for the next shift
explain: Correct: B - bulbar and respiratory muscle involvement in Guillain-Barre is an emergency needing airway planning. A is wrong - feeding risks aspiration. C is wrong - unsupervised swallowing practice is unsafe. D is wrong - waiting a shift is dangerous.

q: A client with myasthenia gravis reports drooping eyelids and difficulty swallowing that worsens with activity. The PN should:
options: Tell the client to push through the fatigue
Report to the RN; worsening weakness may signal myasthenic crisis needing urgent evaluation
Encourage vigorous exercise
Give extra anticholinesterase medication without an order
explain: Correct: B - fatigable weakness progressing to swallowing difficulty can precede respiratory crisis. A is wrong - pushing through worsens myasthenia. C is wrong - vigorous exercise is contraindicated. D is wrong - medication changes need orders; extra doses can cause cholinergic crisis.

q: A client with pernicious anemia reports numbness in the feet and a sore, beefy-red tongue. The PN recognizes these as:
options: Unrelated complaints
Signs of vitamin B12 deficiency needing RN/provider follow-up
Normal aging changes
Side effects of eating too many vegetables
explain: Correct: B - paresthesias and glossitis are classic B12 deficiency signs. A is wrong - they are directly related. C is wrong - they are not normal aging. D is nonsensical.

q: A client with diverticulitis reports left lower quadrant pain and fever. The PN should reinforce that the client should:
options: Eat a high-fiber diet during the acute flare
Follow the prescribed diet (often low residue during flares), take medications as ordered, and report worsening pain, fever, or bleeding
Use a heating pad on high without limits
Ignore the fever
explain: Correct: B - acute diverticulitis is managed with modified diet, ordered meds, and surveillance for complications. A is wrong - high fiber is for prevention, not acute flares. C is wrong - unlimited high heat risks burns. D is wrong - fever suggests infection needing evaluation.

q: A client with peritonitis has a rigid, board-like abdomen with rebound tenderness. The PN should:
options: Palpate the abdomen vigorously to confirm
Keep the client NPO and still, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders
Offer food to test appetite
Encourage ambulation to relieve gas
explain: Correct: B - rigid abdomen with rebound suggests perforation/peritonitis, a surgical emergency. A is wrong - vigorous palpation worsens pain and risks further injury. C is wrong - feeding is contraindicated. D is wrong - ambulation does not treat peritonitis.

q: A client with liver failure becomes confused and has a flapping tremor of the hands. The PN should:
options: Assume the client is uncooperative
Report to the RN immediately; confusion with asterixis suggests hepatic encephalopathy
Offer a high-protein meal
Encourage the client to sleep it off
explain: Correct: B - asterixis with confusion in liver failure is hepatic encephalopathy needing urgent management. A is wrong - this is a neuro change, not behavior. C is wrong - protein is typically restricted in encephalopathy per orders. D is wrong - waiting risks coma.

q: A client with pyelonephritis reports flank pain, fever, and burning urination. The PN's appropriate actions include:
options: Encouraging fluids as ordered, monitoring I&O and temperature, and reporting worsening symptoms to the RN
Telling the client kidney infections resolve without treatment
Restricting all fluids
Stopping the prescribed antibiotics once fever drops
explain: Correct: A - hydration, monitoring, and reporting support treatment of kidney infection. B is wrong - kidney infections need antibiotics and follow-up. C is wrong - fluids help flush bacteria. D is wrong - antibiotics must be completed as prescribed.

q: A client with an ectopic pregnancy reports sudden severe abdominal pain with shoulder pain and dizziness. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client and continue routine monitoring
Recognize possible rupture with internal bleeding, keep the client still, and notify the RN immediately
Encourage the client to walk to relieve the shoulder pain
Offer oral fluids
explain: Correct: B - rupture causes hemorrhage; shoulder pain suggests diaphragmatic irritation from blood, and dizziness signals shock. A is wrong - this is an emergency. C is wrong - ambulation is unsafe with possible hemorrhage. D is wrong - the client may need surgery; NPO is maintained.

q: A laboring client with known placenta previa suddenly has heavy vaginal bleeding and a rigid, tender abdomen. The PN should:
options: Perform a vaginal exam
Keep the client on bed rest, monitor vitals continuously, avoid vaginal exams, and notify the RN immediately for possible abruption
Encourage pushing
Reassure the family that this is normal
explain: Correct: B - rigid tender uterus with bleeding suggests abruptio placentae, an obstetric emergency; exams are contraindicated. A is wrong - vaginal exams can worsen bleeding. C is wrong - pushing is inappropriate and unsafe. D is wrong - this is not normal.

q: A child with croup has a barky cough and inspiratory stridor at rest. The PN should:
options: Give cough syrup and send the child home
Keep the child calm, provide cool mist as ordered, and notify the RN promptly; stridor at rest signals significant airway narrowing
Encourage the child to cry vigorously
Examine the throat with a tongue blade
explain: Correct: B - stridor at rest is concerning; calm, mist, and prompt RN notification are correct. A is wrong - this needs evaluation, not home dismissal. C is wrong - crying worsens airway obstruction. D is wrong - throat examination is for epiglottitis concern, and even then never done casually.

q: A child presents with drooling, tripod positioning, and muffled voice. The PN should:
options: Inspect the throat with a tongue depressor
Keep the child calm and upright, allow the parent to hold the child, avoid throat examination, and notify the RN immediately for possible epiglottitis
Give the child water to help swallowing
Encourage the child to lie flat
explain: Correct: B - the drooling tripod triad suggests epiglottitis; any throat manipulation can cause complete obstruction. A is wrong - never examine the throat. C is wrong - fluids risk aspiration. D is wrong - upright positioning keeps the airway open.

q: Which findings are consistent with atrial fibrillation? Select all that apply.
