options: Irregularly irregular pulse
Fatigue and palpitations
Increased risk of stroke
Regular rapid pulse that never varies
Chest pain that is always present
explain: Correct: A, B, C - irregularly irregular rhythm, palpitations/fatigue, and stroke risk define atrial fibrillation. D is wrong - the hallmark is irregularity, not regularity. E is wrong - chest pain is not always present.

q: Which findings suggest pulmonary embolism that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Sudden dyspnea
Pleuritic chest pain
Tachycardia
Hemoptysis
Gradual ankle swelling over weeks
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - abrupt dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, and hemoptysis are classic PE signs. E is wrong - gradual ankle swelling suggests chronic venous or cardiac issues, not acute PE.

q: Which precautions and findings relate to bacterial meningitis? Select all that apply.
options: Droplet precautions
Severe headache, fever, and nuchal rigidity
Photophobia
Standard precautions only with no isolation
A purpuric rash that does not blanch
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - droplet precautions, the headache/fever/stiff-neck triad, photophobia, and non-blanching purpura (meningococcemia) all relate to bacterial meningitis. D is wrong - standard precautions alone are insufficient.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for inflammatory bowel disease. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will take medications as prescribed even when I feel well
I will report bloody diarrhea, severe pain, or fever
I will follow the diet plan discussed with my provider and dietitian
I should stop all medications during remission
Smoking helps ulcerative colitis so I should start
explain: Correct: A, B, C - adherence, reporting flares, and diet planning are IBD essentials. D is wrong - maintenance therapy often continues in remission per provider. E is wrong - smoking worsens Crohn's disease and is never recommended.

q: Which signs suggest neonatal hypoglycemia that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Jitteriness and tremors
Poor feeding and lethargy
Apnea or cyanosis
Vigorous crying with good tone
Stable temperature with pink color
explain: Correct: A, B, C - jitteriness, poor feeding/lethargy, and apnea are newborn hypoglycemia signs. D and E describe a well newborn, not hypoglycemia.

q: Which findings suggest postpartum depression that the PN must report to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: Persistent sadness and crying beyond the first two weeks
Inability to bond with or care for the baby
Thoughts of harming self or the baby
Mild tearfulness in the first few days after birth
Loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - prolonged sadness, bonding failure, harm thoughts, and anhedonia indicate postpartum depression. D is wrong - brief early tearfulness is typical baby blues, not depression.

q: The PN is reinforcing gout teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will drink plenty of fluids
I will avoid excess alcohol and organ meats
I will take prescribed medications as directed, even between flares
I should stop medication once the pain resolves
Crash dieting will help prevent flares
explain: Correct: A, B, C - hydration, avoiding purine/alcohol triggers, and adherence prevent flares. D is wrong - stopping maintenance therapy invites recurrence. E is wrong - crash dieting can trigger flares.

q: The PN is caring for a client after below-knee amputation. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Monitoring the residual limb for bleeding and signs of infection
Keeping the limb elevated as ordered to reduce swelling
Reinforcing prescribed phantom limb pain management strategies
Reporting severe uncontrolled pain or foul drainage to the RN
Placing a pillow under the knee continuously to prevent contracture
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - bleeding/infection surveillance, elevation, phantom pain strategies, and reporting complications are correct. E is wrong - prolonged knee flexion promotes flexion contracture; positioning follows the rehabilitation plan.

q: A client with diabetes insipidus produces large volumes of dilute urine and reports constant thirst. The PN should:
options: Restrict fluids to reduce urine output
Monitor intake and output closely, watch for dehydration, and report large fluid imbalances to the RN
Encourage the client to ignore the thirst
Document it as normal for diabetes
explain: Correct: B - diabetes insipidus causes massive water loss; the PN tracks I&O, watches for dehydration, and reports. A is wrong - fluid restriction worsens dehydration. C is wrong - thirst signals real fluid need. D is wrong - this is diabetes insipidus (ADH problem), not diabetes mellitus, and it is not normal.

q: The PN is asked to witness the waste of a controlled substance with the RN. This is appropriate because:
options: Wasting requires two licensed nurses per policy, and the PN is a licensed nurse
Only RNs can waste controlled substances
The UAP should do it instead
Wasting is unnecessary
explain: Correct: A - controlled substance wasting requires two licensed nurses to witness; the PN qualifies. B is wrong - PNs are licensed nurses who may witness per policy. C is wrong - UAPs cannot handle controlled substance wasting. D is wrong - wasting is a legal requirement.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client's IV pump alarms 'occlusion' repeatedly. The PN should:
options: Ignore the alarm; the fluid will catch up
Check the tubing for kinks, check the insertion site, and report persistent occlusion to the RN
Increase the infusion rate to push through
Disconnect the tubing to clear it
explain: Correct: B - the PN troubleshoots basic causes (kinks, position, site) and reports unresolved issues. A is wrong - ignoring alarms risks infiltration or missed therapy. C is wrong - the PN never changes rates independently. D is wrong - disconnecting breaks sterility.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching with a client who has low health literacy. The best approach is to:
options: Use complex medical terms to sound professional
Use plain language, visual aids, and teach-back to confirm understanding
Give a lengthy pamphlet without discussion
Speak quickly to cover more material
explain: Correct: B - plain language, visuals, and teach-back ensure comprehension. A is wrong - jargon confuses. C is wrong - pamphlets alone do not confirm understanding. D is wrong - speed reduces comprehension.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: During a procedure, the PN ensures the curtain is closed and the client is properly draped. This demonstrates respect for the client's:
options: Right to refuse
Right to privacy and dignity
Right to a private room
Right to choose the provider
explain: Correct: B - privacy and dignity are protected through draping and curtains. A is about refusal, not exposure. C is wrong - privacy does not require a private room. D is unrelated.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The physical therapist asks the PN to reinforce the client's walking exercises. The PN should:
options: Refuse; therapy is not nursing
Reinforce the exercises as the therapist taught, encouraging the client and reporting difficulties to the RN and therapist
Create new exercises independently
Tell the client to skip therapy when tired
explain: Correct: B - reinforcing the interdisciplinary plan supports recovery; the PN reports problems. A is wrong - collaboration is essential. C is wrong - the PN does not design therapy. D is wrong - skipping therapy without direction harms progress.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is scheduled for discharge but has no ride home. The PN's best action is to:
options: Discharge the client to walk home alone
Report the barrier to the RN/discharge planner so safe transportation can be arranged
Keep the client indefinitely without telling anyone
Call a taxi and pay for it personally
explain: Correct: B - transportation barriers are reported so the discharge team can solve them. A is wrong - unsafe discharge planning. C is wrong - the PN cannot unilaterally extend stays. D is wrong - personal payment is inappropriate and unsustainable.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN documents a late entry for care provided earlier. The correct method is to:
options: Squeeze it into an earlier space in the notes
Label it 'late entry' with the current date and time, and document factually
Back-time it to look on time
Skip documenting since the shift is over
explain: Correct: B - late entries are labeled as such with current date/time; back-timing is falsification. A is wrong - squeezing in entries obscures the record. C is wrong - back-timing is fraud. D is wrong - care must be documented.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family member demands the PN perform a procedure the RN has not assigned. The PN should:
options: Comply to keep the family happy
Explain the PN follows the care plan and assigned tasks, and refer the request to the RN
Argue with the family
Perform the procedure without telling the RN
explain: Correct: B - the PN works within assignments and the care plan, redirecting requests appropriately. A is wrong - family demands do not create assignments. C is wrong - arguing is unprofessional. D is wrong - unassigned procedures break accountability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notices the suction equipment in a client's room is not working. The PN should:
options: Wait for someone else to notice
Report the malfunction per policy, obtain working equipment, and document the actions
Try to repair the electrical components personally
Document that suctioning was done anyway
explain: Correct: B - malfunctioning equipment is reported, replaced, and documented. A is wrong - waiting endangers the client. C is wrong - the PN does not repair electrical devices. D is wrong - false documentation is fraud.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client wants the family involved in all care decisions. The PN should:
options: Exclude the family to save time
Include the family as the client wishes, sharing information the client authorizes
Share all information with the family without asking the client
Tell the client family involvement is not allowed
explain: Correct: B - the client's wishes guide family involvement, with authorized information sharing. A is wrong - excluding desired family is not client-centered. C is wrong - the client's authorization is needed. D is wrong - family involvement is generally welcomed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is prioritizing care for four clients. Using ABCs, which client comes first?
options: A client with a new oxygen saturation of 86% and increased work of breathing
A client with a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg
A client requesting a sleeping pill
A client with a bruise on the arm
explain: Correct: A - airway and breathing always come first; desaturation with distress is the priority. B is elevated but not immediately life-threatening. C and D are routine needs addressed after the emergency.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A dying client is restless and the family is distressed. The PN's best actions include:
options: Telling the family restlessness means recovery
Providing comfort measures per the plan, supporting the family with presence and information, and reporting changes to the RN
Leaving the family alone entirely
Restraining the client to keep them still
explain: Correct: B - end-of-life care centers on comfort, family support, and reporting. A is wrong - false reassurance about recovery is cruel. C is wrong - abandoning the family is not supportive. D is wrong - restraints are inappropriate at end of life.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which situations require immediate RN notification? Select all that apply.
options: A client's systolic blood pressure drops 40 mmHg from baseline with symptoms
New onset of slurred speech and facial droop
A client rates pain 9/10 despite ordered interventions
A client asks for an extra pillow
A stable client's routine vital signs
explain: Correct: A, B, C - symptomatic hypotension, stroke signs, and uncontrolled severe pain all need urgent RN involvement. D and E are routine matters the PN handles independently.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is delegating to the UAP. Which are rights of delegation? Select all that apply.
options: Right task
Right person
Right direction and communication
Right supervision and evaluation
The nurse's accountability ends once the task is delegated
Any task can be delegated to any staff member
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - the five rights of delegation are right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, and right supervision/evaluation. E is wrong - accountability never ends with delegation. F is wrong - only appropriate tasks go to competent staff in stable circumstances.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions are appropriate when a client refuses a medication? Select all that apply.
options: Exploring the reason for refusal
Explaining the purpose and risks of skipping in plain language
Documenting the refusal and reporting it to the RN
Forcing the client to take it
Hiding the medication in food without telling the client
explain: Correct: A, B, C - explore, inform, document, and report respect autonomy. D is wrong - forced medication can be battery. E is wrong - covert administration violates consent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which nursing actions require a provider's order? Select all that apply.
options: Administering a new prescription medication
Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
Starting a new IV infusion
Measuring routine vital signs
Assisting a client with ambulation
explain: Correct: A, B, C - medications, catheter insertion, and IV therapy all require orders. D and E are wrong - vital signs and ambulation assistance are standard nursing functions not requiring individual orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is caring for clients with diverse cultural backgrounds. Which actions show cultural competence? Select all that apply.
options: Asking about food preferences and practices
Accommodating prayer or ritual needs when safe
Learning key phrases in the client's language
Assuming all members of a culture want the same care
Using a qualified interpreter for important teaching
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - asking, accommodating, learning phrases, and using interpreters all show cultural competence. D is wrong - stereotyping ignores individual differences.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which documents must the PN verify are complete before a surgical client leaves the unit? Select all that apply.
options: Signed consent
Pre-op checklist including NPO, allergies, and site marking
History and physical on the chart
The client's restaurant menu choices
Anesthesia assessment as required by policy
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - consent, safety checklist, H&P, and anesthesia assessment are required pre-op documentation. D is wrong - menu choices are irrelevant to surgical readiness.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing burn prevention in the kitchen. The key teaching point is:
options: Keep pot handles turned inward and never leave cooking unattended
Let children play near the stove to learn respect for heat
Use water on a grease fire
Carry hot liquids over children's heads
explain: Correct: A - inward handles and attended cooking prevent scalds and burns. B is wrong - children near stoves risk serious burns. C is wrong - water spreads grease fires; smother or use an extinguisher. D is wrong - carrying hot liquids over children invites spills.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing firearm safety for a family. The correct teaching is to:
options: Keep loaded guns accessible for protection
Store firearms unloaded, locked, with ammunition locked separately
Let children handle guns to remove curiosity
Store guns loaded but hidden
explain: Correct: B - unloaded, locked, with ammunition separate is the safe storage standard. A is wrong - accessible loaded guns cause tragedies. C is wrong - unsupervised handling is never safe. D is wrong - hidden but loaded is still accessible and dangerous.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing drowning prevention. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: Children can be left briefly in the pool if they can float
An adult actively supervises children near water, with pool fencing and locked gates
Floaties make children drown-proof
Swimming lessons eliminate all drowning risk
explain: Correct: B - active adult supervision plus barriers is the prevention standard. A is wrong - children drown silently in seconds. C is wrong - floaties are not safety devices. D is wrong - lessons reduce but never eliminate risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing carbon monoxide safety. The key teaching includes:
options: CO detectors on every level, never running generators indoors, and never warming cars in closed garages
CO is harmless in small amounts
Only older homes need detectors
Opening a window makes indoor generator use safe
explain: Correct: A - detectors plus eliminating indoor combustion sources prevents CO poisoning. B is wrong - CO is dangerous at low levels. C is wrong - all homes need detectors. D is wrong - windows do not make generator use safe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A parent asks about choking prevention for a toddler. The PN reinforces:
options: Grapes and hot dogs are safe whole for toddlers
Cutting round foods into small pieces, avoiding nuts and hard candy, and supervising meals
Letting toddlers eat while running
Propping bottles for convenience
explain: Correct: B - small pieces, avoiding high-risk foods, and supervision prevent choking. A is wrong - whole grapes and hot dogs are classic choking hazards. C is wrong - eating while active increases aspiration risk. D is wrong - propped bottles risk choking and ear infections.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN finds a toddler has swallowed a button battery. The PN's priority is to:
options: Wait for it to pass naturally
Seek emergency care immediately; button batteries cause rapid esophageal burns
Give bread to push it down
Induce vomiting
explain: Correct: B - button batteries cause severe tissue burns within hours; this is an emergency. A is wrong - waiting risks perforation. C is wrong - food does not dislodge batteries safely. D is wrong - vomiting can cause additional injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing space heater safety. The correct teaching includes:
options: Placing heaters near curtains for warmth
Keeping heaters 3 feet from anything flammable, never leaving them unattended, and plugging directly into the wall
Using extension cords to reach far rooms
Leaving heaters on overnight unattended
explain: Correct: B - clearance, supervision, and direct wall plugs prevent fires. A is wrong - curtains ignite easily. C is wrong - extension cords overheat. D is wrong - unattended heaters are a leading fire cause.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing emergency planning for a client dependent on home oxygen. The key teaching is:
options: No planning is needed; power never fails
Notify the power company of the medical need, keep backup tanks, and have a plan to relocate if power fails
Use candles during outages
Turn the oxygen up during outages to stockpile
explain: Correct: B - medical-needs registration, backup supply, and a relocation plan keep oxygen-dependent clients safe. A is wrong - outages happen. C is wrong - open flames near oxygen are dangerous. D is wrong - flow rates follow orders, not stockpiling.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces playground safety. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: Children should play on any equipment regardless of age recommendations
Use age-appropriate equipment, supervise actively, and check for hot surfaces and hazards
Playgrounds need no supervision for school-age children
Broken equipment is fine if children are careful
explain: Correct: B - age-appropriate equipment, supervision, and hazard checks prevent injuries. A is wrong - equipment is age-graded for safety. C is wrong - supervision is still needed. D is wrong - broken equipment must be reported and avoided.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which items belong in a home emergency kit? Select all that apply.
options: Water and nonperishable food
Flashlight with extra batteries
A list of medications and medical contacts
Important documents in a waterproof container
Perishable leftovers for the first day
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - water, food, light, medication lists, and protected documents are kit essentials. E is wrong - perishables spoil without refrigeration.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces tornado safety. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Going to the lowest level, away from windows
Sheltering in an interior room or closet
Covering the head and neck
Opening windows to equalize pressure
Sheltering under highway overpasses
explain: Correct: A, B, C - lowest level, interior rooms, and protecting head/neck are tornado safety basics. D is wrong - opening windows wastes time and does not help. E is wrong - overpasses are dangerous wind tunnels.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which measures prevent burns from hot liquids in a care setting? Select all that apply.
options: Testing water temperature before bathing clients
Keeping hot drinks away from clients at risk of spills
Using lids on hot beverage cups
Serving soup at boiling temperature
Placing hot items within reach of confused clients
explain: Correct: A, B, C - temperature checks, spill prevention, and lids prevent scald burns. D is wrong - boiling soup scalds. E is wrong - hot items must be kept from confused clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces Tdap vaccine teaching for an adult who never received it. The key point is:
options: Tdap is only for children
One Tdap dose is recommended for adults never vaccinated, then Td or Tdap boosters per schedule
Tetanus vaccines are unnecessary after childhood
Tdap prevents the flu
explain: Correct: B - unvaccinated adults need one Tdap, then routine boosters. A is wrong - adults need pertussis protection too. C is wrong - tetanus boosters continue lifelong. D is wrong - Tdap covers tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis, not flu.

q: The PN reinforces breastfeeding benefits. Which statement is correct?
options: Formula is identical to breast milk in every way
Breast milk provides ideal nutrition and antibodies, and breastfeeding benefits maternal health
Breastfeeding has no maternal benefits
Breast milk increases infection risk
explain: Correct: B - breast milk offers tailored nutrition, antibodies, and maternal benefits like faster recovery. A is wrong - formula does not replicate antibodies. C is wrong - maternal benefits are well established. D is wrong - breast milk protects against infection.

q: A parent asks when honey can be given to an infant. The PN reinforces:
options: Honey is safe from birth
No honey before 12 months due to botulism risk
Honey is fine after 6 months
Only raw honey is dangerous
explain: Correct: B - infant botulism risk means no honey before age 1. A is wrong - newborns are most vulnerable. C is wrong - 6 months is still too early. D is wrong - all honey carries the risk for infants.

q: The PN reinforces introducing solid foods. The correct teaching is:
options: Start solids at 2 months
Introduce solids around 6 months, one at a time, while continuing breast milk or formula
Replace all milk feedings with solids at 4 months
Start with honey-sweetened cereal
explain: Correct: B - around 6 months, single foods introduced gradually alongside milk feedings. A is too early. C is wrong - milk remains primary nutrition through the first year. D is wrong - honey is prohibited before 12 months.

q: The PN reinforces breast self-awareness teaching. The key point is:
options: Monthly self-exams replace mammograms
Know what is normal for your breasts and report changes such as lumps, skin changes, or nipple discharge to the provider promptly
Only providers can notice breast changes
Breast changes never need reporting
explain: Correct: B - self-awareness with prompt reporting of changes supports early detection. A is wrong - self-exam supplements, not replaces, screening. C is wrong - clients often find their own changes. D is wrong - changes always warrant evaluation.

q: An older adult asks about vision and hearing. The PN reinforces:
options: Vision and hearing loss are untreatable so screening is pointless
Regular vision and hearing screenings help catch treatable problems early
Only the young need sensory screening
Glasses and hearing aids never help
explain: Correct: B - many sensory problems are treatable when caught early. A is wrong - cataracts, glaucoma, and hearing loss often respond to treatment. C is wrong - older adults need screening most. D is wrong - corrective devices substantially help.

q: Which infant feeding practices should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Breast milk or formula as the primary nutrition for the first year
No cow's milk as a main drink before 12 months
Iron-fortified formula when not breastfeeding
Honey in the bottle to soothe
Propping the bottle for convenience
explain: Correct: A, B, C - breast milk or iron-fortified formula for the first year, no cow's milk as a main drink before 12 months. D is wrong - honey risks botulism. E is wrong - propped bottles risk choking and ear infections.

q: The PN reinforces adolescent nutrition teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Calcium and vitamin D for bone growth
Iron-rich foods, especially for menstruating teens
Limiting sugary drinks
Skipping breakfast to control weight
Energy drinks as a daily beverage
explain: Correct: A, B, C - calcium, iron, and limited sugar support teen growth. D is wrong - skipping meals impairs growth and learning. E is wrong - energy drinks risk excess caffeine and sugar.

q: A client blames a speeding ticket on the faulty speedometer rather than speeding. This is an example of:
options: Rationalization
Denial
Sublimation
Compensation
explain: Correct: A - rationalization creates a logical excuse for behavior. B is wrong - the client admits the ticket happened. C is wrong - nothing productive is created. D is wrong - no weakness is being offset.

q: A client focuses on detailed medical statistics to avoid feeling fear about a diagnosis. This is an example of:
options: Intellectualization
Regression
Displacement
Projection
explain: Correct: A - intellectualization uses facts and logic to distance from emotion. B is wrong - there is no return to earlier behavior. C is wrong - no emotion is redirected at another target. D is wrong - feelings are not attributed to others.

q: A client who cannot play sports due to injury becomes a dedicated team coach. This is an example of:
options: Compensation
Denial
Regression
Rationalization
explain: Correct: A - compensation offsets a limitation by excelling in a related area. B is wrong - the injury is acknowledged. C is wrong - there is no return to childlike behavior. D is wrong - no excuse is being made.

q: A client with obsessive-compulsive disorder must perform lengthy rituals before eating. The PN's best approach is to:
options: Interrupt the rituals to save time
Allow time for rituals within the plan, avoid punishment, and report changes to the RN
Ridicule the rituals to motivate stopping
Forbid all rituals immediately
explain: Correct: B - rituals reduce overwhelming anxiety; the plan accommodates them while therapy progresses, and changes are reported. A is wrong - abrupt interruption spikes anxiety. C is wrong - ridicule is abusive. D is wrong - forbidding rituals without a therapeutic plan is harmful.

q: A client with PTSD becomes distressed by a loud noise on the unit. The PN's best initial action is to:
options: Ignore the reaction
Ensure safety, speak calmly, reduce triggers, and report to the RN
Tell the client the reaction is overblown
Restrain the client immediately
explain: Correct: B - safety, calm reassurance, trigger reduction, and reporting are the trauma-informed response. A is wrong - ignoring distress is not therapeutic. C is wrong - minimizing trauma reactions is harmful. D is wrong - restraints are a last resort for imminent danger.

q: Seclusion is being considered for a violent client. The PN understands that seclusion:
options: Can be used whenever staff feel like it
Is a last resort requiring a provider order, with continuous monitoring and reporting
Needs no documentation
Can be decided by the PN alone
explain: Correct: B - seclusion requires an order, is time-limited, and needs close monitoring and documentation. A is wrong - it is never casual. C is wrong - extensive documentation is required. D is wrong - the PN cannot order seclusion.

q: Which PN responses are nontherapeutic and should be avoided? Select all that apply.
options: Giving unsolicited advice
Offering false reassurance
Asking 'why' questions that sound judgmental
Changing the subject when the client expresses feelings
Using open-ended questions
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - advice, false reassurance, judgmental 'why' questions, and subject-changing all block therapeutic communication. E is wrong - open-ended questions are therapeutic and should be used.

q: Which approaches support a client with obsessive-compulsive disorder? Select all that apply.
options: Maintaining a structured routine
Allowing reasonable time for rituals per the care plan
Praising non-ritual behaviors
Punishing ritual behaviors
Reporting increased anxiety or ritual frequency to the RN
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - structure, accommodation per plan, positive reinforcement, and reporting changes support OCD care. D is wrong - punishment increases anxiety and is nontherapeutic.

q: A client with dysphagia is prescribed thickened liquids. The PN should:
options: Serve thin water since it is easier to drink
Ensure liquids are thickened to the prescribed consistency and the client is upright
Allow the client to drink lying flat
Skip the thickener to improve taste
explain: Correct: B - prescribed thickness plus upright positioning prevents aspiration. A is wrong - thin liquids are aspirated most easily. C is wrong - flat positioning invites aspiration. D is wrong - skipping thickener defeats the swallowing plan.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is applying a condom catheter. The correct practice includes:
options: Applying it tightly to prevent leaks
Sizing correctly, leaving space at the tip, securing snugly without constriction, and monitoring skin
Leaving it on for a week without removal
Using adhesive directly on irritated skin
explain: Correct: B - proper sizing, tip space, snug-not-tight securement, and skin monitoring prevent injury. A is wrong - tight application impairs circulation. C is wrong - daily removal and skin checks are needed. D is wrong - adhesive on irritated skin worsens breakdown.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes warfarin and is at bleeding risk. The PN should use which razor for shaving?
options: A straight razor for a close shave
An electric razor to reduce nick risk
A dull disposable razor
No shaving is ever allowed
explain: Correct: B - electric razors minimize cuts in clients with bleeding risk. A is wrong - straight razors cut easily. C is wrong - dull blades cause more nicks. D is wrong - shaving is allowed with safe equipment.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is logrolling a client with spinal precautions. The correct technique is:
options: Turning the head first, then the body
Moving the body as one unit with enough staff to keep the spine aligned
Bending the spine to turn faster
Logrolling alone without help
explain: Correct: B - the spine stays aligned by moving the body as a unit with adequate staff. A is wrong - the head must not turn separately. C is wrong - bending risks cord injury. D is wrong - logrolling requires multiple staff.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Before ambulating a client who has been on bed rest, the PN should:
options: Have the client stand and walk immediately
Dangle the client at the bedside, assess for dizziness, then stand with assistance
Carry the client to the chair
Skip dangling to save time
explain: Correct: B - dangling assesses orthostatic tolerance before standing, preventing falls. A is wrong - immediate standing risks syncope. C is wrong - carrying is unsafe for both. D is wrong - skipping assessment invites falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a male client with a urinal. The correct practice includes:
options: Leaving the urinal in place indefinitely
Providing privacy, placing the urinal correctly, and removing it promptly after use with perineal care as needed
Forcing fluids to fill it quickly
Placing it without explanation
explain: Correct: B - privacy, correct placement, prompt removal, and hygiene preserve dignity and skin. A is wrong - prolonged contact irritates skin. C is wrong - forcing fluids is inappropriate. D is wrong - explanation reduces anxiety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has frequent diarrhea. The PN's priority skin intervention is to:
options: Scrub the area with harsh soap
Cleanse gently after each episode, pat dry, and apply barrier cream per orders
Leave the area uncleaned to avoid irritation
Apply powder heavily into skin folds
explain: Correct: B - gentle cleansing plus barrier protection prevents moisture breakdown. A is wrong - harsh soap damages skin. C is wrong - stool left on skin causes breakdown. D is wrong - heavy powder cakes and irritates.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions support communication with a client who has hearing loss? Select all that apply.
options: Facing the client when speaking
Speaking clearly at a moderate pace
Reducing background noise
Shouting from another room
Covering the mouth while talking
explain: Correct: A, B, C - facing, clear speech, and quiet environments aid lip-reading and hearing. D is wrong - shouting distorts speech and startles. E is wrong - covering the mouth blocks visual cues.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which comfort measures are appropriate for a client with fever? Select all that apply.
options: Light coverings rather than heavy blankets
Encouraging fluids as permitted
Monitoring temperature and reporting per protocol
Applying ice baths routinely
Bundling the client in heavy blankets to sweat it out
explain: Correct: A, B, C - light covers, fluids, and monitoring manage fever safely. D is wrong - ice baths cause shivering and are not routine. E is wrong - bundling raises temperature dangerously.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help stimulate appetite in a hospitalized client? Select all that apply.
options: Providing oral care before meals
Reducing unpleasant odors
Offering small, frequent meals as ordered
Encouraging the client to eat in bed flat on the back
Rushing the client through meals
explain: Correct: A, B, C - mouth care, pleasant environment, and small frequent meals encourage eating. D is wrong - flat positioning risks aspiration. E is wrong - rushing reduces intake.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes amlodipine and reports ankle swelling. The PN should:
options: Tell the client to stop the drug immediately
Document and report the edema to the RN; peripheral edema is a known calcium channel blocker effect
Reassure the client that swelling is a sign it is working
Advise doubling the dose
explain: Correct: B - ankle edema is a common amlodipine effect needing provider review. A is wrong - the PN does not stop prescribed drugs. C is wrong - edema is a side effect, not efficacy. D is wrong - dose changes need orders.

q: A client takes apixaban. The most important teaching the PN should reinforce is to:
options: Stop it before any dental work without telling anyone
Report any unusual bleeding or bruising immediately and tell all providers about the anticoagulant
Take it only when feeling ill
Double the dose if a dose is missed
explain: Correct: B - bleeding surveillance and informing every provider are critical with anticoagulants. A is wrong - stopping needs provider direction. C is wrong - it is scheduled therapy. D is wrong - missed doses follow provider/pharmacist guidance, never doubling.

q: A client taking clopidogrel is scheduled for surgery. The PN should:
options: Tell the client to keep taking it through surgery
Report the clopidogrel use to the RN; antiplatelets are often held before surgery per provider orders due to bleeding risk
Stop it independently a week before
Double the dose to prevent clots during surgery
explain: Correct: B - the surgical team must know about antiplatelets; holding decisions belong to the provider. A is wrong - continuing may be unsafe. C is wrong - the PN does not stop drugs independently. D is wrong - doubling increases bleeding risk.

q: The PN is reinforcing aspirin teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will take it on an empty stomach for faster action
I will take it with food, and report ringing in the ears, stomach pain, or black stools
I can take as much as I want since it is over the counter
Aspirin has no bleeding risk
explain: Correct: B - food protects the stomach; tinnitus, pain, and melena signal toxicity or bleeding. A is wrong - empty-stomach aspirin irritates the mucosa. C is wrong - OTC does not mean unlimited. D is wrong - bleeding is aspirin's major risk.

q: A client takes omeprazole. The PN reinforces that it should be taken:
options: At bedtime with food
Before breakfast, since proton pump inhibitors work best before the day's acid production
Only when heartburn occurs
With antacids at the same time
explain: Correct: B - PPIs are most effective taken before the first meal. A is wrong - bedtime with food is less effective. C is wrong - PPIs are daily therapy, not as-needed. D is wrong - antacids can interfere; timing is separated.

q: A client with hepatic encephalopathy takes lactulose. The PN reinforces that the expected effect is:
options: No bowel changes
Two to three soft stools daily, which helps remove ammonia
Severe watery diarrhea constantly
Complete constipation
explain: Correct: B - lactulose's goal is 2-3 soft stools daily to excrete ammonia. A is wrong - no effect means the dose needs provider review. C is wrong - constant watery diarrhea causes dehydration and electrolyte loss. D is the opposite of the goal.

q: The order is for 75 mg of a medication; available: 50 mg/mL. How many mL should the PN administer?
options: 1.5 mL
2.5 mL
3 mL
explain: Correct: B - 75 mg divided by 50 mg/mL = 1.5 mL. A, C, and D reflect calculation errors.

q: An IV of 500 mL is ordered to infuse over 4 hours. What is the rate in mL/hr?
options: 100 mL/hr
125 mL/hr
150 mL/hr
200 mL/hr
explain: Correct: B - 500 mL divided by 4 hours = 125 mL/hr. A, C, and D reflect arithmetic errors.

q: The PN is reinforcing lispro insulin teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Take it with meals, since it acts very quickly
Be alert for hypoglycemia soon after the dose
It can be taken hours after eating with the same effect
Always carry a fast-acting carbohydrate
Skipping the meal after the dose is safe
explain: Correct: A, B, D - rapid-acting lispro is mealtime insulin with quick hypoglycemia risk, so fast carbs must be handy. C is wrong - timing with meals is essential. E is wrong - skipping the meal after dosing causes hypoglycemia.

q: The PN is reinforcing glargine insulin teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Take it at the same time each day
It has no pronounced peak
It must never be mixed with other insulins
It causes hypoglycemia mainly at its 6-hour peak
Doubling the dose when glucose is high is safe
explain: Correct: A, B, C - glargine is a once-daily basal insulin with flat action that is never mixed. D is wrong - there is no pronounced peak. E is wrong - dose changes need provider orders.

q: The PN is reinforcing spironolactone teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Report muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat
Avoid salt substitutes containing potassium
Have potassium levels monitored as ordered
Eat as many potassium-rich foods as possible
It is safe to combine with any other diuretic without telling the provider
explain: Correct: A, B, C - spironolactone spares potassium, so hyperkalemia signs, salt substitutes, and lab monitoring matter. D is wrong - excess potassium intake is dangerous. E is wrong - diuretic combinations need provider oversight.

q: The PN is reinforcing epinephrine auto-injector teaching for severe allergies. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Use it at the first sign of a severe allergic reaction
Call emergency services after use
Hold it in place for the recommended seconds per the device instructions
Report the use to the provider promptly
Keep it in a hot car for easy access
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - early use, emergency call, proper hold time, and provider notification are essential. E is wrong - heat degrades epinephrine; it needs room-temperature storage.

q: A client's BUN is 42 mg/dL and creatinine is 2.1 mg/dL (both elevated). The PN should:
options: Document them as normal
Report them to the RN promptly; rising BUN and creatinine suggest kidney dysfunction
Encourage a high-protein diet
Tell the client the kidneys are fine
explain: Correct: B - BUN (normal ~7-20) and creatinine (normal ~0.6-1.2) this high indicate renal impairment needing evaluation. A is wrong - both exceed normal. C is wrong - protein intake follows provider/dietitian direction in kidney dysfunction. D is wrong - reassurance contradicts the labs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client taking warfarin has an INR of 4.5. The PN should:
options: Give the next warfarin dose as usual
Hold the dose per protocol and report to the RN; INR 4.5 exceeds the usual 2.0-3.0 therapeutic range, raising bleeding risk
Double the dose to bring it down
Document it as therapeutic
explain: Correct: B - supratherapeutic INR needs holding per protocol and provider notification. A is wrong - dosing through a high INR risks hemorrhage. C is wrong - more warfarin worsens it. D is wrong - 4.5 is above therapeutic range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a bronchoscopy with sedation, the PN should check which finding before offering fluids?
options: Pedal pulses
Return of the gag reflex
Bowel sounds
Deep tendon reflexes
explain: Correct: B - throat anesthesia requires gag reflex return before oral intake to prevent aspiration. A, C, and D are unrelated to bronchoscopy recovery.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a colonoscopy with polyp removal, which finding must the PN report immediately?
options: Mild cramping and passing gas
Heavy rectal bleeding
Drowsiness from sedation
A small amount of clear drainage
explain: Correct: B - heavy rectal bleeding after polypectomy suggests hemorrhage or perforation. A is expected post-procedure. C is expected sedation recovery. D is not characteristic; bleeding is the concern.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a liver biopsy, which PN actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Positioning the client on the right side as ordered
Monitoring vital signs closely for bleeding
Reporting severe abdominal pain or hypotension to the RN
Encouraging vigorous activity immediately
Keeping the client NPO until fully alert if sedated
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - right-side pressure, vital sign surveillance, reporting bleeding signs, and NPO until alert are correct. D is wrong - rest, not vigorous activity, follows liver biopsy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which measures help prevent aspiration? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the head of the bed elevated during and after meals
Checking the gag reflex after procedures involving throat anesthesia
Following NPO orders before procedures
Ensuring swallowing precautions are followed for at-risk clients
Offering fluids to a client who cannot swallow safely
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - elevation, gag checks, NPO compliance, and swallowing precautions all prevent aspiration. E is wrong - fluids are contraindicated when swallowing is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which laboratory values are critical and must be reported immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Glucose 35 mg/dL
Potassium 6.3 mEq/L
Hemoglobin 6.8 g/dL
Platelets 25,000/mm3
Sodium 140 mEq/L
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - severe hypoglycemia, hyperkalemia, severe anemia, and critical thrombocytopenia are all critical values. E is wrong - sodium 140 is within the normal 135-145 range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A pre-op client's blood pressure is 190/120 mmHg with a severe headache. The PN should:
options: Proceed to surgery as scheduled
Report to the RN immediately; severe hypertension may require postponing elective surgery
Give the client's home antihypertensive without an order
Tell the client headaches are normal before surgery
explain: Correct: B - severe preoperative hypertension with symptoms needs provider evaluation; surgery may be delayed. A is wrong - proceeding ignores a serious risk. C is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope. D is wrong - this headache signals hypertensive urgency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is reviewing labs before a procedure. The platelet count is 28,000/mm3. The PN should:
options: Document it as normal
Report it to the RN promptly; severe thrombocytopenia raises bleeding risk for invasive procedures
Tell the client to eat more protein
Proceed with the procedure without mentioning it
explain: Correct: B - platelets of 28,000 (normal 150,000-400,000) are critically low and must be communicated before invasive procedures. A is wrong - this is severely abnormal. C is wrong - diet does not fix acute thrombocytopenia. D is wrong - silence endangers the client.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is NPO for an afternoon procedure and keeps asking for water. The PN's best response is to:
options: Give small sips since it is the afternoon
Explain the reason for NPO, offer mouth swabs or ice chips only if permitted by orders, and report continued requests to the RN
Tell the client to stop complaining
Document that the client is noncompliant
explain: Correct: B - empathetic explanation with permitted comfort measures maintains NPO safety. A is wrong - sips violate NPO. C is wrong - dismissing the client is nontherapeutic. D is wrong - requesting water is not noncompliance.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client reports brief episodes of slurred speech and one-sided weakness that resolve within an hour. The PN should recognize these as:
options: Normal fatigue
Transient ischemic attacks, warning signs of stroke needing immediate RN notification
Low blood sugar only
Anxiety attacks
explain: Correct: B - TIAs are stroke warnings; urgent evaluation is needed even though symptoms resolve. A is wrong - focal neuro symptoms are never normal fatigue. C is wrong - glucose may be checked, but TIA is the priority concern. D is wrong - one-sided weakness is not anxiety.

q: A client describes sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back. The PN should:
options: Offer an antacid
Keep the client still, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders; this suggests aortic dissection
Encourage coughing
Document it for the next shift
explain: Correct: B - tearing chest-to-back pain is the classic aortic dissection presentation, a surgical emergency. A is wrong - antacids do not treat dissection. C is wrong - coughing is irrelevant and potentially harmful. D is wrong - waiting is fatal.

q: A client with hemophilia needs blood drawn. The PN should:
options: Use a large-bore needle without concern
Use the smallest needle possible, apply prolonged pressure afterward, and report unusual bleeding to the RN
Avoid all blood draws forever
Apply a tight tourniquet for an extended time
explain: Correct: B - minimizing trauma and ensuring hemostasis with prolonged pressure protects hemophilia clients. A is wrong - large bores increase bleeding. C is wrong - necessary labs are still drawn with precautions. D is wrong - prolonged tourniquets cause hematomas.

q: A young woman reports a butterfly-shaped rash across her cheeks, joint pain, and fatigue. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Measles
Systemic lupus erythematosus, which should be reported to the RN for workup
Contact dermatitis only
Normal sun exposure
explain: Correct: B - malar rash with arthralgia and fatigue suggests lupus needing evaluation. A is wrong - measles rash is morbilliform with high fever. C is wrong - contact dermatitis does not cause systemic joint pain. D is wrong - this pattern is not normal sun effect.

q: A client's leg shows expanding redness, warmth, and swelling with red streaks. The PN should:
options: Mark the border, monitor, and report to the RN promptly; spreading redness suggests cellulitis
Ignore it as a bruise
Apply heat and wait a week
Lance the area at the bedside
explain: Correct: A - expanding erythema with streaking is cellulitis needing prompt treatment; marking tracks spread. B is wrong - this is not a simple bruise. C is wrong - waiting a week risks sepsis. D is wrong - the PN never incises tissue.

q: A client develops hives, wheezing, and hypotension after an IV medication. The PN's first actions are to:
options: Continue the infusion and observe
Stop the infusion, call for help, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders for anaphylaxis
Give oral fluids
Document it as a mild reaction
explain: Correct: B - hives with wheezing and hypotension is anaphylaxis; stop the trigger, get help, and prepare for epinephrine per orders. A is wrong - continuing the infusion worsens the reaction. C is wrong - oral fluids do not treat anaphylaxis. D is wrong - this is severe, not mild.

q: A pregnant client has severe nausea and vomiting with weight loss and dehydration. The PN should:
options: Tell her morning sickness is always harmless
Report to the RN; hyperemesis gravidarum needs evaluation and fluid/electrolyte management
Advise her to eat large meals
Suggest she avoid all fluids
explain: Correct: B - hyperemesis with dehydration and weight loss is not normal morning sickness and needs treatment. A is wrong - this exceeds normal nausea. C is wrong - large meals worsen vomiting. D is wrong - fluid avoidance worsens dehydration.

q: The PN is reinforcing gestational diabetes teaching. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I do not need any glucose testing in pregnancy
I will complete the glucose screening as ordered and follow the diet and monitoring plan
Diabetes in pregnancy never affects the baby
I can eat unlimited sweets since the baby needs sugar
explain: Correct: B - screening plus diet and monitoring manage gestational diabetes. A is wrong - screening is standard. C is wrong - uncontrolled glucose risks macrosomia and other complications. D is wrong - sweets sabotage glucose control.

q: A client with severe preeclampsia is at risk for seizures. The PN's priority safety measures include:
options: Leaving the client unattended to rest
Keeping the environment quiet and dim, having seizure precautions in place, and reporting changes to the RN immediately
Encouraging bright lights and stimulation
Giving magnesium sulfate without an order
explain: Correct: B - seizure precautions with low stimulation and close monitoring protect the client. A is wrong - unattended seizure risk is dangerous. C is wrong - stimulation can trigger seizures. D is wrong - magnesium requires orders and RN management.

q: A client at 32 weeks reports regular contractions every 8 minutes with pelvic pressure. The PN should:
options: Reassure her that preterm labor cannot be stopped
Report to the RN immediately; regular contractions before 37 weeks suggest preterm labor needing evaluation
Tell her to go for a long walk
Advise bed rest without notifying anyone
explain: Correct: B - regular contractions at 32 weeks need urgent assessment for preterm labor. A is wrong - interventions may delay delivery. C is wrong - walking is not the intervention. D is wrong - the RN must be notified.

q: A client at 38 weeks reports a gush of fluid from the vagina. The PN's first actions are to:
options: Perform a vaginal exam to check dilation
Note the time, color, and odor of the fluid, monitor maternal and fetal status, avoid vaginal exams, and notify the RN
Tell the client it is probably urine
Send the client home
explain: Correct: B - suspected membrane rupture needs assessment of fluid characteristics, monitoring, and RN notification; exams are minimized to reduce infection. A is wrong - exams increase infection risk after ROM. C is wrong - dismissal without assessment is unsafe. D is wrong - evaluation is needed first.

q: A postpartum client on day 3 has a temperature of 101.8 F, foul-smelling lochia, and uterine tenderness. The PN should:
options: Reassure her this is normal
Report to the RN promptly; these suggest postpartum infection (endometritis)
Encourage her to douche
Tell her to wait a week
explain: Correct: B - fever with foul lochia and tenderness indicates endometritis needing treatment. A is wrong - these are not normal findings. C is wrong - douching is contraindicated postpartum. D is wrong - waiting risks sepsis.

q: An infant with RSV bronchiolitis has increased work of breathing and poor feeding. The PN should:
options: Encourage large feedings to keep strength up
Keep the infant's airway clear with bulb suction as ordered, monitor respiratory status closely, and report worsening distress to the RN
Place the infant flat on the back without monitoring
Give cough medicine without an order
explain: Correct: B - suctioning, close respiratory monitoring, and reporting are correct for bronchiolitis. A is wrong - large feedings risk aspiration with distress. C is wrong - positioning and monitoring matter. D is wrong - medicating without orders exceeds scope.

q: A 4-week-old has projectile vomiting after feedings and a palpable olive-shaped mass in the abdomen. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Normal spit-up
Pyloric stenosis, needing prompt RN/provider notification
Colic that needs no report
Overfeeding only
explain: Correct: B - projectile vomiting with an olive mass is classic pyloric stenosis. A is wrong - projectile vomiting is not normal spit-up. C is wrong - colic does not cause projectile vomiting or a mass. D is wrong - the mass indicates obstruction, not overfeeding.

q: A toddler has intermittent severe abdominal pain, draws the knees to the chest, and passes currant-jelly stools. The PN should:
options: Offer a large meal to comfort the child
Report immediately; these suggest intussusception, a surgical emergency
Give an enema without an order
Wait to see if it resolves
explain: Correct: B - colicky pain with currant-jelly stools is intussusception until proven otherwise. A is wrong - feeding is contraindicated. C is wrong - enemas need orders (and air enemas are therapeutic, done by providers). D is wrong - waiting risks bowel necrosis.

q: Which findings are warning signs of stroke that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Facial droop
Arm weakness or drift
Slurred speech
Sudden severe headache
Mild indigestion
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - FAST signs plus sudden severe headache are stroke warnings. E is wrong - indigestion is not a stroke sign.

q: Which actions are correct in anaphylaxis? Select all that apply.
options: Stopping the triggering infusion or exposure
Calling for help and notifying the RN immediately
Preparing for epinephrine administration per orders
Keeping the client supine with legs elevated if hypotensive
Giving the client oral fluids to dilute the allergen
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - stop the trigger, get help, prepare epinephrine, and position for shock. E is wrong - oral fluids do not treat anaphylaxis and risk aspiration.

q: The PN is reinforcing lupus teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Avoiding excessive sun exposure
Taking medications as prescribed even when feeling well
Reporting increased joint pain, rash, or fever
Getting regular rest and avoiding known triggers
Stopping all medications during remission without direction
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - sun protection, adherence, flare reporting, and rest/trigger avoidance manage lupus. E is wrong - stopping meds without provider direction invites flares.

q: Which safety measures are appropriate for a client with hemophilia? Select all that apply.
options: Using a soft toothbrush and electric razor
Avoiding contact sports and high-risk activities
Applying prolonged pressure after venipuncture
Reporting any unusual bleeding immediately
Using aspirin for pain relief
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - gentle hygiene, activity precautions, prolonged pressure, and bleeding surveillance protect hemophilia clients. E is wrong - aspirin impairs platelets and is avoided.

q: The PN is reinforcing gestational diabetes teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Following the prescribed meal plan
Monitoring blood glucose as instructed
Keeping prenatal appointments for fetal monitoring
Reporting very high or low readings promptly
Skipping insulin doses when feeling well
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - meal planning, glucose monitoring, prenatal surveillance, and prompt reporting manage gestational diabetes. E is wrong - insulin is never skipped without provider direction.

q: Which signs of preterm labor should the PN teach clients to report? Select all that apply.
options: Regular contractions before 37 weeks
Pelvic pressure or low back ache
Fluid leaking from the vagina
Vaginal bleeding
Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - regular contractions, pressure, fluid leak, and bleeding are preterm labor warnings. E is wrong - mild dependent edema alone is common in pregnancy.

q: Which measures help prevent RSV transmission that the PN should reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Frequent hand hygiene
Avoiding close contact with sick individuals
Cleaning toys and surfaces
Keeping infants away from tobacco smoke
Sharing cups to build immunity
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - hand hygiene, avoiding sick contacts, clean surfaces, and smoke-free air reduce RSV risk. E is wrong - sharing cups spreads infection.

q: The PN made a documentation error by writing the wrong time. The correct way to fix it is to:
options: Erase it completely
Draw a single line through the error, write 'error,' initial and date it, then document correctly
Cover it with correction fluid
Rewrite the entire page
explain: Correct: B - a single line-through with 'error,' initials, and date keeps the record transparent and legal. A is wrong - erasing obscures the record. C is wrong - correction fluid is never used in medical records. D is unnecessary and impractical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is writing a nursing note. Which abbreviation should be avoided?
options: q4h
U for units
mg
PO
explain: Correct: B - 'U' is on the do-not-use list because it is mistaken for zero, causing tenfold overdoses; write 'units.' A, C, and D are standard acceptable abbreviations.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: After a client falls, the PN's documentation should include:
options: Who was at fault for the fall
Objective facts: time, location, what was found, assessments, notifications, and interventions
A promise it will never happen again
The PN's opinion about the client's clumsiness
explain: Correct: B - factual documentation supports care and legal defense. A is wrong - fault-finding does not belong in the chart. C is wrong - promises cannot be made. D is wrong - opinions about the client are inappropriate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Two staff members discuss a client's case in a crowded elevator. The PN should:
options: Join the discussion
Remind them that public areas are not appropriate for client discussions and suggest a private location
Report them to the police immediately
Ignore it; elevators are fine
explain: Correct: B - the PN protects confidentiality by redirecting the conversation privately. A is wrong - joining violates confidentiality. C is wrong - police are not the first step; education and policy handle it. D is wrong - public discussions breach privacy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: In an emergency, a provider orders a procedure on an unconscious client without consent. The PN understands this is acceptable under:
options: The provider's personal preference
Implied consent for emergency treatment when the client cannot consent and no surrogate is available
The PN's authorization
No legal basis at all
explain: Correct: B - implied consent covers emergency lifesaving treatment for clients unable to consent. A is wrong - preference is not a legal basis. C is wrong - the PN does not authorize procedures. D is wrong - implied consent is well established in law.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with chronic pain reports the current regimen is not working. The PN's best advocacy action is to:
options: Tell the client to accept the pain
Document the pain reports objectively and report them to the RN/provider for reassessment
Increase the pain medication independently
Suggest the client seek care elsewhere
explain: Correct: B - advocacy means communicating the client's unrelieved pain through proper channels with objective data. A is wrong - dismissing pain abandons the client. C is wrong - the PN cannot change orders. D is wrong - referring away avoids the problem.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is giving an SBAR report about a hypotensive client. The 'R' (recommendation) should sound like:
options: I think the client looks bad
I recommend you come evaluate the client now; the blood pressure is 82/50 with dizziness
The client has always had low pressure
Maybe someone should check sometime
explain: Correct: B - a clear, specific recommendation with data drives action. A is vague. C is irrelevant history. D is passive and unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to supervise a UAP performing a task the UAP has never done. The PN should:
options: Let the UAP figure it out alone
Verify the UAP's competence first, provide direction, and supervise closely
Do the task without teaching the UAP
Assign a different task the UAP is competent to perform
explain: Correct: B - delegation requires verifying competence, clear direction, and supervision. A is wrong - unsupervised unfamiliar tasks endanger clients. C misses the teaching opportunity but is safer than A; B is best. D is also acceptable, but B directly addresses safe delegation of the needed task.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client in restraints needs toileting, fluids, and repositioning. The PN's monitoring responsibilities include:
options: Checking once per shift
Frequent checks of circulation, skin, and basic needs per policy, with documentation and reporting to the RN
Removing restraints without an order when busy
Tightening restraints to prevent all movement
explain: Correct: B - restrained clients need frequent monitoring, need-meeting, documentation, and RN communication. A is wrong - once per shift is neglectful. C is wrong - discontinuation needs orders. D is wrong - restraints must never impair circulation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A Spanish-speaking client needs teaching reinforced. No interpreter is immediately available. The PN should:
options: Use the bilingual housekeeper to interpret
Use approved translation resources or a phone interpreter service, and request a qualified interpreter
Skip the teaching
Speak English loudly until the client nods
explain: Correct: B - approved language resources and qualified interpreters ensure accurate communication. A is wrong - untrained ad hoc interpreters risk errors and privacy breaches. C is wrong - teaching cannot be skipped. D is wrong - volume does not overcome language barriers.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is prioritizing morning care. Which client should be seen first?
options: A stable client awaiting discharge paperwork
A client with new-onset confusion and a blood glucose of 38 mg/dL
A client requesting a shower
A client with chronic back pain rated 3/10
explain: Correct: B - severe hypoglycemia with neuro changes is the emergency. A, C, and D are stable or routine needs addressed afterward.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client asks the PN to help them write a living will. The PN's best action is to:
options: Draft the legal document independently
Provide general information, encourage discussion with family and provider, and refer to appropriate resources per policy
Refuse to discuss it
Tell the client living wills are unnecessary
explain: Correct: B - the PN provides information and referrals; legal drafting belongs to the client and proper resources. A is wrong - the PN does not draft legal documents. C is wrong - refusing abandons the client's need. D is wrong - it dismisses a valid planning tool.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which findings should the PN report to the charge RN before the end of the shift? Select all that apply.
options: A client's new pressure injury discovered during the shift
A fall that occurred, even without injury
A medication that the client refused
A client who ate 100% of lunch
A family complaint about care
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - new skin breakdown, falls, refusals, and complaints all need RN awareness and follow-up. D is wrong - good appetite is a positive finding needing no escalation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions protect the PN legally? Select all that apply.
options: Practicing within scope and competence
Documenting accurately and promptly
Following provider orders that are clear and safe
Carrying out an order the PN believes is unsafe without question
Maintaining confidentiality
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - scope adherence, good documentation, safe orders, and confidentiality are legal protections. D is wrong - blindly following unsafe orders creates liability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is preparing to administer a high-risk medication. Which safety checks apply? Select all that apply.
options: Two-nurse verification per policy
Checking the order, dose calculation, and client identity
Reviewing allergies and relevant labs
Skipping checks to save time during a busy shift
Having the UAP double-check the dose
explain: Correct: A, B, C - independent double checks, order/dose/identity verification, and allergy/lab review prevent errors. D is wrong - busyness never justifies skipping checks. E is wrong - UAPs do not verify medications.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which scenarios represent appropriate PN advocacy? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting unrelieved pain to the provider
Requesting an interpreter for a non-English-speaking client
Ensuring a client's cultural dietary needs are met
Making medical decisions for an incapacitated client without a surrogate
Arranging a family meeting the client requested
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - pain reporting, language access, cultural needs, and facilitating requested meetings are advocacy. D is wrong - the PN does not make medical decisions for clients; surrogates and providers do.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which tasks are within PN scope when caring for a post-op client? Select all that apply.
options: Monitoring vital signs and reporting changes
Reinforcing coughing and deep breathing
Changing the sterile dressing per orders
Removing the surgical drains independently without an order
Advancing the diet beyond the ordered progression
explain: Correct: A, B, C - monitoring, pulmonary hygiene reinforcement, and ordered dressing changes are PN roles. D is wrong - drain removal needs an order. E is wrong - diet advancement follows orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which handoff elements are essential for a client receiving frequent PRN pain medication? Select all that apply.
options: Last dose time and effectiveness
Current pain rating and trend
Total doses in the shift
The client's favorite foods
Sedation level and respiratory status
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - last dose, pain trend, totals, and sedation/respiratory status ensure safe continued management. D is wrong - food preferences are irrelevant to pain handoff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing wheelchair safety. The key points include:
options: Lock the wheels before transfers and keep footrests positioned to prevent falls
Leave the wheels unlocked for quick movement
Remove the footrests permanently
Transfer without locking to save time
explain: Correct: A - locked wheels and proper footrests prevent tip and fall injuries during transfers. B is wrong - unlocked chairs roll away. C is wrong - footrests support feet and prevent dragging. D is wrong - skipping locks is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing concussion teaching for a teen athlete. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I can return to play the same day if I feel okay
I will report headache, dizziness, or confusion and sit out until medically cleared
Helmets prevent all concussions
Concussions are not serious
explain: Correct: B - symptom reporting and medical clearance before return-to-play are the standard. A is wrong - same-day return risks second-impact injury. C is wrong - helmets reduce but do not prevent concussions. D is wrong - concussions are brain injuries.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces heat illness prevention for outdoor workers. The teaching includes:
options: Drink water regularly, take shade breaks, and recognize dizziness, nausea, and confusion as warning signs
Avoid all fluids to prevent sweating
Work through dizziness
Dark urine means hydration is adequate
explain: Correct: A - hydration, rest breaks, and warning-sign recognition prevent heat stroke. B is wrong - fluid avoidance causes heat illness. C is wrong - dizziness needs immediate rest and cooling. D is wrong - dark urine signals dehydration.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing candle safety. The correct teaching is:
options: Leave candles burning overnight for ambiance
Never leave burning candles unattended, keep them from flammables, and use sturdy holders
Place candles near curtains
Let children light candles unsupervised
explain: Correct: B - supervision, clearance, and stable holders prevent fires. A is wrong - unattended candles are a top fire cause. C is wrong - curtains ignite easily. D is wrong - children need supervision with fire.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces lightning safety. The correct teaching includes:
options: Shelter under a lone tree
Go indoors to a substantial building, avoid open fields and water, and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder
Use a corded phone during the storm
Lie flat in an open field
explain: Correct: B - indoor shelter away from water and open areas is the standard. A is wrong - lone trees attract strikes. C is wrong - corded phones conduct electricity. D is wrong - open fields are dangerous.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces earthquake safety (drop, cover, hold on). During shaking, the PN should teach clients to:
options: Run outside during the shaking
Drop under sturdy furniture, cover the head and neck, and hold on
Stand in a doorway on an upper floor
Use elevators to evacuate
explain: Correct: B - drop, cover, and hold on protects from falling objects. A is wrong - running during shaking causes injuries. C is wrong - doorways are not the safest spot in modern buildings. D is wrong - elevators are dangerous in earthquakes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is teaching parents never to shake a baby. The reason to reinforce is:
options: Shaking is an effective discipline method
Shaking can cause brain injury, bleeding, and death
Babies enjoy vigorous shaking
Shaking helps babies sleep
explain: Correct: B - shaken baby syndrome causes devastating brain injury. A is wrong - shaking is abuse, not discipline. C and D are dangerously false.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing home oxygen tank safety. The correct teaching includes:
options: Lay tanks on their sides for easy access
Secure tanks upright so they cannot fall, away from heat
Store tanks near the furnace
Transport tanks loose in the car trunk
explain: Correct: B - secured upright tanks cannot become projectiles if the valve breaks; heat is avoided. A is wrong - fallen tanks with broken valves become dangerous projectiles. C is wrong - heat near oxygen is a fire risk. D is wrong - loose tanks roll and can break valves.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces fireworks safety for teens. The key teaching is:
options: Homemade fireworks are safe with adult supervision
Leave fireworks to professionals; never hold lit fireworks or relight duds
Sparklers are safe for toddlers
Point fireworks at friends for fun
explain: Correct: B - professional displays are the safe option; holding lit fireworks and relighting duds cause severe injuries. A is wrong - homemade fireworks are illegal and dangerous. C is wrong - sparklers burn hot enough to cause serious burns. D is wrong - aiming at people is never safe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which chemical safety practices should the PN reinforce for homes with children? Select all that apply.
options: Storing chemicals in locked cabinets
Keeping products in original labeled containers
Never mixing bleach with ammonia
Storing chemicals in food containers for convenience
Keeping the poison control number accessible
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - locked storage, original labels, no bleach-ammonia mixing (toxic gas), and poison control access prevent poisonings. D is wrong - food containers invite accidental ingestion.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which measures help prevent frostbite that the PN should reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Dressing in warm layers with dry socks and gloves
Limiting time outdoors in extreme cold and wind
Seeking shelter at the first signs of numbness or pale skin
Warming frostbitten areas with hot water
Drinking alcohol to stay warm
explain: Correct: A, B, C - layers, limited exposure, and early shelter prevent frostbite. D is wrong - hot water burns numb tissue; gradual lukewarm warming is correct. E is wrong - alcohol increases heat loss.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reviewing active threat response (run, hide, fight). The correct teaching includes: Select all that apply.
options: Running to safety if it can be done safely
Hiding, locking/barricading doors, and silencing phones
Fighting as a last resort if confronted
Pulling the fire alarm to warn everyone
Seeking personal belongings before leaving
explain: Correct: A, B, C - run, hide, fight is the standard response sequence. D is wrong - alarms can draw people into danger and are not the alert method. E is wrong - belongings are never worth delaying escape.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces MMR vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: MMR is only for international travelers
MMR protects against measles, mumps, and rubella per the childhood schedule
One dose in adulthood erases the need for childhood doses
MMR treats active measles
explain: Correct: B - MMR is routine childhood immunization against all three diseases. A is wrong - it is for all children, not just travelers. C is wrong - the childhood series is the foundation. D is wrong - vaccines prevent, not treat.

q: A parent asks about the varicella vaccine. The PN reinforces that:
options: Natural chickenpox infection is safer than the vaccine
The vaccine prevents chickenpox and is part of the routine childhood schedule
The vaccine is only for adults
Chickenpox is harmless so prevention is unnecessary
explain: Correct: B - vaccination prevents chickenpox and its complications per schedule. A is wrong - natural infection risks pneumonia, encephalitis, and shingles later. C is wrong - it is primarily a childhood vaccine. D is wrong - chickenpox can be serious.

q: A parent asks about milk for a 14-month-old. The PN reinforces:
options: Whole cow's milk is fine before 12 months as the main drink
After 12 months, whole milk can be introduced; low-fat milk is usually recommended after age 2
Only chocolate milk provides calcium
Toddlers should drink a gallon of milk daily
explain: Correct: B - whole milk after 12 months, transitioning to low-fat after 2 per guidance. A is wrong - cow's milk as a main drink before 12 months risks iron deficiency and GI blood loss. C is wrong - plain milk provides calcium without added sugar. D is wrong - excess milk displaces other nutrients.

q: The PN reinforces the importance of breakfast for school-age children. The best teaching is:
options: Skipping breakfast improves concentration
A nutritious breakfast supports learning and growth
Only sugary cereals provide energy
Children never need breakfast
explain: Correct: B - breakfast fuels morning learning and growth. A is wrong - skipping impairs concentration. C is wrong - sugary cereals cause energy crashes. D is wrong - breakfast matters for children.
